Related Articles Special Features 4 Times Couture Fashion Designers Took Their Talents to the Stage Halston, Christian Dior, Pierre Cardin, and Isaac Mizrahi all started in the fashion industry but took a turn at Broadway costume design. By Talaura Harms June 01, 2021 Halston, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Liza Minnelli and Gower Champion Bob Deutsch Ryan Murphy’s Netflix series Halston culminates [spoiler alert] with the fashion designer creating the costumes for Martha Graham’s 1987 dance work Persephone at City Center. Halston had previously sold his brand to Esmark, Inc., and in doing so, was prevented from releasing any designs branded as a Halston. Earlier in the series, the character of Halston sneers at the world of theatrical costuming—both with his colleague Joe Eula’s costume design for Got Tu Go Disco and when meeting John David Ridge, the costumer turned fashion designer who would eventually replace Halston as the head of the brand bearing his name. However, this Episode Five collaboration with Graham (played by Mary Beth Peil) wasn’t his first foray into the field. Not only had Halston had a years-long friendship and working relationship with Graham, his deep friendship with Liza Minnelli ( Krysta Rodriguez in the series ) led to his sole Broadway credit as costume designer for the 1977 John Kander, Fred Ebb, and George Furth musical The Act , starring Minnelli decked out in Halston sequined jumpsuits. (Fun fact: The Act also happens to be director Martin Scorcese’s single Broadway credit.) Click through the gallery below for a look back at Halston\'s designs. Read on for a few other times couture designers turned their spindles toward Broadway for costume design. And not just for Josephine Baker’s gowns (looking at you, Balenciaga). Pierre Cardin Paris couturier Pierre Cardin once designed suits for The Beatles, and was well-known for his avant-garde flair and Space Age fashion. He favored geometric shapes and created the “bubble dress.” But in 1963, Cardin was credited for the execution of the ladies’ costumes for the period romance The Lady of Camellias , adapted by Terrance McNally from Alexandre Dumas’ La Dame aux Camélias (also the source material for Verdi’s La Traviata ). The production was directed by famous film director Franco Zeffirelli and starred Susan Strasberg as Camille. Despite three Tony nominations, including one for Marcel Escoffier’s costume design, it only ran for 13 performances. Susan Strasberg in The Lady of the Camellias Friedman-Abeles/©NYPL for the Performing Arts Christian Dior Just after WWII, Christian Dior founded his own Paris design house and created what became known as the “New Look.” His designs were more voluminous than women had worn during the fabric-rationing war years—incorporating wasp-waist corsets, with hip padding and petticoats under fuller longer skirts. In 1960 he is credited for the Women’s Costume Designs for the Broadway adaptation of Giraudoux’s Duel of Angels , starring Vivien Leigh. The play is set in southern France in 1868, but Dior infuses the gown designs with his own “New Look” adding pleats and volume to the period pieces. Isaac Mizrahi American designer Isaac Mizrahi attended the High School of Performing Arts before going on to Parsons School of Design, so it’s no stretch for him to step into the theatre world for costume design. He launched his first couture collection in 1987 and had a multi-million dollar diffusion line at Target in the early 2000s. His first Broadway costume design was for the 2001 revival of Clare Booth Luce’s 1936 comedy of manners The Women, winning a Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Costume Design . He added two additional Broadway credits in 2006 with designs for both Barefoot in the Park and The Threepenny Opera. Amy Ryan, Jennifer Coolidge, Lisa Emery, Cynthia Nixon and Lynn Collins in Broadway\'s The Women , 2001 Joan Marcus It’s Reversible Special mentions must go to two costume designers who also made names for themselves in the fashion industry: Bob Mackie and Emilio Sosa . Bob Mackie Mackie’s career began as a sketch artist for the costumers at Paramount Studios, but he quickly moved to designer. His work in the film industry led to an invitation in 1966 from Mitzi Gaynor to design her costumes for upcoming Las Vegas cabarets and television specials, which in turn led to his hire by The Carol Burnett Show. Mackie remained costumer designer for all eleven seasons of the series, creating everything from the sequined gowns Burnett wore in the show closings to the Scarlet O\'Hara parody curtain(rod) gown. His first costume for Cher was her appearance on The Carol Burnett Show; he would go on to costume her for The Sonny and Cher Show. Mackie\'s first Broadway design was for the 1971 revival of On the Town, followed by Carol Channing\'s costumes for Lorelei. After years of dressing celebrities on stage and for the red carpet (especially Cher), he released a ready-to-wear collection in 1982. Mackie won his first Tony in 2019 for, of course, The Cher Show. Emilio Sosa Raised in New York City, Sosa attended Art and Design High School before studying Fashion Design at Pratt Institute. He made his Broadway debut in 2002 with the costume design for Topdog/Underdog. Sosa has a string of theatrical credits, including four additional Broadway shows (with a Tony nomination for The Gershwin\'s Porgy and Bess ), The Alvin Ailey Dance Company, and The Rockettes. In 2010, Sosa was a contestant on the fashion design competition series Project Runway , finishing as runner-up and creating what would become his own label, esosa. He returned for the second season of Project Runway All Stars, again winning runner-up honors. Sosa hasn\'t left the theatre industry though. The Yellowstone County Sheriff’s Office seized the dogs , 37 Newfoundlands and five Australian Shepherds, at the residence Sept. 25. Deputy Yellowstone County Attorney Ingrid Rosenquist said Saturday their trials are pending, and she cannot release additional details about the case. The dogs, which were found malnourished with lice and worms, have been recovering since the raid. As of Saturday, 20 dogs are staying under a tent on a county-owned property in Billings, 15 are living at the Montana Women’s Prison and seven have been returned to their original owners. Vanessa Willardson Tent where 20 dogs are staying as of Saturday Many of dogs will be under the care of Newfoundland Club of America Rescue Network in a few weeks. According to Rosenquist, the remaining dogs will not be up for adoption until they are given sufficient care through the network. “They\'re going to continue the veterinary work that that\'s been given to them with the sheriff\'s office here, if necessary, and spay and neuter them. Vanessa Willardson Ingrid Rosenquist Captain Kent O’Donnell with the Yellowstone County Sheriff’s Office said Saturday morning that the dogs have collectively gained 300 pounds since they were seized. “During the daytime, we have a lot of help. Vanessa Willardson He also gave credit to the surrounding community for the dogs’ quick recovery. “We\'ve had so much support from the community, from the public. I think we\'ve taken in about $4,000 in donations from just people sending $10, $20 checks to the Sheriff\'s Office, which has been great, which will take a lot of the financial responsibility off the county taxpayers. But the local businesses have been great on this,” said O’Donnell. He thanked Clarity Animal Hospital, Best Friends Animal Hospital and Montana Mobile Vet for providing veterinarian services. Vanessa Willardson Captain Kent O\'Donnell “We had a lot of ear infections, lots of skin irritation and skin problems that needed medication for that. So, it\'s been a constant, constant battle getting medications for all the dogs. We\'re on our third round of worming, which has been an ordeal,” said O’Donnell. Related Articles Special Features 4 Times Couture Fashion Designers Took Their Talents to the Stage Halston, Christian Dior, Pierre Cardin, and Isaac Mizrahi all started in the fashion industry but took a turn at Broadway costume design. By Talaura Harms June 01, 2021 Halston, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Liza Minnelli and Gower Champion Bob Deutsch Ryan Murphy’s Netflix series Halston culminates [spoiler alert] with the fashion designer creating the costumes for Martha Graham’s 1987 dance work Persephone at City Center. Halston had previously sold his brand to Esmark, Inc., and in doing so, was prevented from releasing any designs branded as a Halston. Earlier in the series, the character of Halston sneers at the world of theatrical costuming—both with his colleague Joe Eula’s costume design for Got Tu Go Disco and when meeting John David Ridge, the costumer turned fashion designer who would eventually replace Halston as the head of the brand bearing his name. However, this Episode Five collaboration with Graham (played by Mary Beth Peil) wasn’t his first foray into the field. Not only had Halston had a years-long friendship and working relationship with Graham, his deep friendship with Liza Minnelli ( Krysta Rodriguez in the series ) led to his sole Broadway credit as costume designer for the 1977 John Kander, Fred Ebb, and George Furth musical The Act , starring Minnelli decked out in Halston sequined jumpsuits. (Fun fact: The Act also happens to be director Martin Scorcese’s single Broadway credit.) Click through the gallery below for a look back at Halston\'s designs. Read on for a few other times couture designers turned their spindles toward Broadway for costume design. And not just for Josephine Baker’s gowns (looking at you, Balenciaga). Pierre Cardin Paris couturier Pierre Cardin once designed suits for The Beatles, and was well-known for his avant-garde flair and Space Age fashion. He favored geometric shapes and created the “bubble dress.” But in 1963, Cardin was credited for the execution of the ladies’ costumes for the period romance The Lady of Camellias , adapted by Terrance McNally from Alexandre Dumas’ La Dame aux Camélias (also the source material for Verdi’s La Traviata ). The production was directed by famous film director Franco Zeffirelli and starred Susan Strasberg as Camille. Despite three Tony nominations, including one for Marcel Escoffier’s costume design, it only ran for 13 performances. Susan Strasberg in The Lady of the Camellias Friedman-Abeles/©NYPL for the Performing Arts Christian Dior Just after WWII, Christian Dior founded his own Paris design house and created what became known as the “New Look.” His designs were more voluminous than women had worn during the fabric-rationing war years—incorporating wasp-waist corsets, with hip padding and petticoats under fuller longer skirts. In 1960 he is credited for the Women’s Costume Designs for the Broadway adaptation of Giraudoux’s Duel of Angels , starring Vivien Leigh. The play is set in southern France in 1868, but Dior infuses the gown designs with his own “New Look” adding pleats and volume to the period pieces. Isaac Mizrahi American designer Isaac Mizrahi attended the High School of Performing Arts before going on to Parsons School of Design, so it’s no stretch for him to step into the theatre world for costume design. He launched his first couture collection in 1987 and had a multi-million dollar diffusion line at Target in the early 2000s. His first Broadway costume design was for the 2001 revival of Clare Booth Luce’s 1936 comedy of manners The Women, winning a Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Costume Design . He added two additional Broadway credits in 2006 with designs for both Barefoot in the Park and The Threepenny Opera. Amy Ryan, Jennifer Coolidge, Lisa Emery, Cynthia Nixon and Lynn Collins in Broadway\'s The Women , 2001 Joan Marcus It’s Reversible Special mentions must go to two costume designers who also made names for themselves in the fashion industry: Bob Mackie and Emilio Sosa . Bob Mackie Mackie’s career began as a sketch artist for the costumers at Paramount Studios, but he quickly moved to designer. His work in the film industry led to an invitation in 1966 from Mitzi Gaynor to design her costumes for upcoming Las Vegas cabarets and television specials, which in turn led to his hire by The Carol Burnett Show. Mackie remained costumer designer for all eleven seasons of the series, creating everything from the sequined gowns Burnett wore in the show closings to the Scarlet O\'Hara parody curtain(rod) gown. His first costume for Cher was her appearance on The Carol Burnett Show; he would go on to costume her for The Sonny and Cher Show. Mackie\'s first Broadway design was for the 1971 revival of On the Town, followed by Carol Channing\'s costumes for Lorelei. After years of dressing celebrities on stage and for the red carpet (especially Cher), he released a ready-to-wear collection in 1982. Mackie won his first Tony in 2019 for, of course, The Cher Show. Emilio Sosa Raised in New York City, Sosa attended Art and Design High School before studying Fashion Design at Pratt Institute. He made his Broadway debut in 2002 with the costume design for Topdog/Underdog. Sosa has a string of theatrical credits, including four additional Broadway shows (with a Tony nomination for The Gershwin\'s Porgy and Bess ), The Alvin Ailey Dance Company, and The Rockettes. In 2010, Sosa was a contestant on the fashion design competition series Project Runway , finishing as runner-up and creating what would become his own label, esosa. He returned for the second season of Project Runway All Stars, again winning runner-up honors. Sosa hasn\'t left the theatre industry though. The Yellowstone County Sheriff’s Office seized the dogs , 37 Newfoundlands and five Australian Shepherds, at the residence Sept. 25. Watch to see how the dogs are being cared for: Yellowstone County community helps 42 neglected dogs recover after Shepherd raid The two sisters tied to the case, Katie Marie Milliken and Rebekkah Lynn Collins, are each facing 14 charges of animal cruelty. A newly surfaced clip on social media claims to reveal Efron’s original demo vocals for High School Musical ’s Get’cha Head in the Game , and fans can’t stop reacting. The short video, posted Tuesday, features the actor performing the song during the movie’s famous basketball scene. The post reads, “20 years after the release we can finally hear his voice. With the date from June 2005 the song has some different adlibs and the instrumental was still under production.” While Efron played basketball star Troy Bolton in the 2006 Disney Channel hit, the vocals used in the film were actually recorded by actor and singer Drew Seeley. The demo appears to show what Efron’s voice sounded like before that switch, and the reactions online have been mixed. “Okay this isn’t the worst but it shows how much he really improved in the later films,” one fan commented, adding that Efron “lowkey owes Drew Seeley for this starting point in his career.” Others were more direct, with one writing, “This sounds a mess,” and another exclaiming, “Thank god for Drew Seeley cause omfg my ears!!!!!! They bleeding!!!!” Some even pointed out that the leaked clip makes it clear why Seeley’s vocals were chosen. “No way, that’s why they gave the job to Drew Seeley,” one fan wrote. Efron went on to record his own songs for High School Musical 2 (2007) and High School Musical 3: Senior Year (2008), as well as in the hit musical film Hairspray . Drew Seeley, who originally auditioned for the role of Troy, later told E! News that there were no hard feelings, explaining that Efron was “better suited” for the part because of his chemistry with Vanessa Hudgens. Director Kenny Ortega also shed light on the decision, revealing to Entertainment Tonight that “the songs were written before Zac got the role.” Ortega said that while Efron “had a lovely voice,” it didn’t fit what the songs required at the time. “So he sang everything, and then we dubbed parts of it so that it had greater vocal strength,” Ortega explained. “But the second movie and the third movie, everything was written for him. And that’s important for people to know, that Zac Efron did sing.” Now, nearly two decades later, fans are hearing that early version for the first time, and whether they love it or not, it’s a fascinating glimpse into how far Efron’s voice, and career, have come since High School Musical first aired. We\'re excited to bring a new look at the unconventional blend of ideas to Collider\'s Exclusive Preview event for upcoming winter film and television releases, though it doesn\'t spotlight the faux Claus. Instead, it shows Breckenridge\'s love interest, played by Cross \'s Ryan Eggold , alongside Sister, Sister star Tia Mowry , who\'ll put her plans in jeopardy. Our still finds Matthew (Eggold) and Natascha (Mowry) coupled up just outside the resort and looking a bit romantic themselves . Like Breckenridge\'s scheming Taylor, Natascha will be in close proximity to the Sun Peaks manager throughout the film, as the trailer shows she\'ll be digging into the origins of their mystery Santa once Taylor starts raising suspicion. If she also has an interest in Matthew, she might just thwart Taylor in more ways than one. Regardless of whether sparks begin flying for them or not, her presence is more than enough to raise the stakes of the mom\'s humorous holiday hoax . My Secret Santa follows Taylor as she tries desperately to find a way to pay for her daughter\'s acceptance into the elite snowboarding camp at the Sun Peaks resort. With the help of some loved ones, she undergoes a transformation into a rosy-cheeked older gentleman with a big white beard to rival the real St Nick . "Hugh Mann" quickly lands a gig as the resort\'s Santa and becomes a sensation despite some near-misses. It\'s all going better than Taylor could\'ve imagined, until she starts falling for Matthew , the man she once rejected and now spends time with in her working hours. Complications from their chemistry threaten to upend her entire Santa scheme and a prospective relationship. Rounding out this Christmas tale are Madison MacIsaac and Diana Maria Riva . \'My Secret Santa\' Director Is a Netflix Holiday Romance Favorite my-secret-santa-netflix Adding to the excitement for My Secret Santa is the man behind the camera — Mike Rohl . He\'s responsible for masterminding one of Netflix\'s defining Christmas romance trilogies in The Princess Switch , starring Vanessa Hudgens as both a Chicago baker and a duchess who swap lives around the holidays and end up forever intertwined. In more recent years, he\'s continued the trend of making seasonal love stories , like Bringing Christmas Home and Hallmark\'s Falling Together . Joining him on his latest holiday venture are writers Carley Smale and Ron Oliver and producers Howard and Alexander Braunstein . My Secret Santa comes down the chimney onto Netflix on December 3. Not only is silver practically a neutral, but the suspended glitter in the polish also adds an expensive feel to the look. Cardi sparked engagement rumors when a diamond ring was spotted on her left hand in some of the images that she shared of the new baby. She has yet to comment on her current relationship status with Diggs. But, in the meantime, she has a new piece of gold jewelry — made from her baby’s umbilical cord — that she can wear on repeat. Instead of a divorcee attempting to win his kids back by disguising himself as a matronly, caring nanny in the Robin Williams classic , however, this feature casts Alexandra Breckenridge as a single mom seeking extra cash by disguising herself as the perfect St. Nick for a luxury ski resort. We\'re excited to bring a new look at the unconventional blend of ideas to Collider\'s Exclusive Preview event for upcoming winter film and television releases, though it doesn\'t spotlight the faux Claus. Instead, it shows Breckenridge\'s love interest, played by Cross \'s Ryan Eggold , alongside Sister, Sister star Tia Mowry , who\'ll put her plans in jeopardy. Our still finds Matthew (Eggold) and Natascha (Mowry) coupled up just outside the resort and looking a bit romantic themselves . Like Breckenridge\'s scheming Taylor, Natascha will be in close proximity to the Sun Peaks manager throughout the film, as the trailer shows she\'ll be digging into the origins of their mystery Santa once Taylor starts raising suspicion. If she also has an interest in Matthew, she might just thwart Taylor in more ways than one. Regardless of whether sparks begin flying for them or not, her presence is more than enough to raise the stakes of the mom\'s humorous holiday hoax . My Secret Santa follows Taylor as she tries desperately to find a way to pay for her daughter\'s acceptance into the elite snowboarding camp at the Sun Peaks resort. With the help of some loved ones, she undergoes a transformation into a rosy-cheeked older gentleman with a big white beard to rival the real St Nick . "Hugh Mann" quickly lands a gig as the resort\'s Santa and becomes a sensation despite some near-misses. It\'s all going better than Taylor could\'ve imagined, until she starts falling for Matthew , the man she once rejected and now spends time with in her working hours. Complications from their chemistry threaten to upend her entire Santa scheme and a prospective relationship. Rounding out this Christmas tale are Madison MacIsaac and Diana Maria Riva . \'My Secret Santa\' Director Is a Netflix Holiday Romance Favorite my-secret-santa-netflix Adding to the excitement for My Secret Santa is the man behind the camera — Mike Rohl . He\'s responsible for masterminding one of Netflix\'s defining Christmas romance trilogies in The Princess Switch , starring Vanessa Hudgens as both a Chicago baker and a duchess who swap lives around the holidays and end up forever intertwined. In more recent years, he\'s continued the trend of making seasonal love stories , like Bringing Christmas Home and Hallmark\'s Falling Together . Joining him on his latest holiday venture are writers Carley Smale and Ron Oliver and producers Howard and Alexander Braunstein . My Secret Santa comes down the chimney onto Netflix on December 3. On October 30, the reality TV star shared a video of her latest manicure on Instagram, and like a moth to a flame, I couldn’t look away. The look was a perfect mix of glam and drama, yet still practical, thanks to the simple yet elegant finish she chose. To start, extensions were applied to Kardashian’s nails for extra length. They were then cut and filed into an almond shape before being painted a glittery silver. A magnet was then used to bring out the real star of the show, the cat eye effect that made it look like they came to life under different types of lighting. The gorgeous color felt glam enough to catch eyes and spark conversation, yet was subtle enough for me to consider it a serious contender for a 2025 holiday manicure. Khloe Kardashian showing her silver cat eye nails. (Image credit: Getty Images) Cat eye polishes are the perfect manicure for those who want their nails to look a little more glam, without spending too much extra time at the nail salon. The magic of this look lies in the polish itself, allowing you to achieve a highly detailed manicure without worrying about nail charms falling off, snagging, or matching the designs on your fingers with your outfit. Not only is silver practically a neutral, but the suspended glitter in the polish also adds an expensive feel to the look. His movies often began with negative box office results and critical reviews but garnered appreciation over time. Films like “The Thing,” “They Live,” and “Prince of Darkness” exemplify this trend. However, his last film, “The Ward,” has not yet received such a rediscovery. Rediscovering “The Ward”: A Hidden Gem “The Ward” is currently streaming on platforms such as Prime Video, Peacock, and Tubi. Despite being absent from collections like the Criterion Channel’s “Directed by John Carpenter,” many argue it is Carpenter’s best work since “They Live” in 1988. Overview of the Film Set in a psychiatric hospital in 1966 Oregon, “The Ward” follows the story of Kristen, played by Amber Heard. She arrives after being rescued from a house fire but remembers nothing before the incident. Her interactions with Dr. Stringer, portrayed by Jared Harris, are fraught with tension. Kristen (Amber Heard): The lead character struggling with memory loss. Dr. Stringer (Jared Harris): The psychiatric doctor overseeing Kristen’s care. Emily (Mamie Gummer): The rebellious patient. Sarah (Danielle Panabaker): The flirtatious ward member. Iris (Lyndsy Fonseca): The artistic one. Zoey (Laura-Leigh): The childlike ward resident. As the plot unfolds, Kristen encounters a menacing ghost that threatens her and the other patients. The screenplay by Michael and Shawn Rassmussen provides a basic horror framework, focusing primarily on the haunting atmosphere and character interactions. Cinematography and Direction Carpenter’s direction ensures that “The Ward,” while not exceptionally frightening, maintains momentum. His use of 35mm cinematography preserves its visual appeal, as viewers follow Kristen through the hospital’s dark corridors. Limited special effects allow Carpenter’s talent for composition to shine through, resulting in engaging visual storytelling. A Cast of Women Unlike many of Carpenter’s prior works, “The Ward” features a predominantly female cast. This shift offers a refreshing perspective within the horror genre. Amber Heard’s performance as Kristen adds depth to the character, navigating elements of slasher and noir styles. Reception and Cultural Context Upon its premiere at the Toronto Film Festival, “The Ward” struggled to find a significant audience during its commercial release in summer 2011. Released shortly after the theatrically mismanaged “Sucker Punch,” it received minimal attention, relegating it to a swift home-video distribution. Even with its lack of initial acclaim, “The Ward” stands as a confident entry in Carpenter’s later work. It serves as a thoughtful conclusion to his big-screen horror contributions, inviting viewers to explore themes of trauma and resilience. Now, horror fans have the opportunity to reclaim this overlooked film. Where to Watch “The Ward” is available for streaming on: Prime Video Peacock Tubi As audiences continue to discover John Carpenter’s underrated film, “The Ward,” it might finally achieve the recognition it deserves. His movies often began with negative box office results and critical reviews but garnered appreciation over time. Films like “The Thing,” “They Live,” and “Prince of Darkness” exemplify this trend. However, his last film, “The Ward,” has not yet received such a rediscovery. Rediscovering “The Ward”: A Hidden Gem “The Ward” is currently streaming on platforms such as Prime Video, Peacock, and Tubi. Despite being absent from collections like the Criterion Channel’s “Directed by John Carpenter,” many argue it is Carpenter’s best work since “They Live” in 1988. Overview of the Film Set in a psychiatric hospital in 1966 Oregon, “The Ward” follows the story of Kristen, played by Amber Heard. She arrives after being rescued from a house fire but remembers nothing before the incident. Her interactions with Dr. Stringer, portrayed by Jared Harris, are fraught with tension. Kristen (Amber Heard): The lead character struggling with memory loss. Dr. Stringer (Jared Harris): The psychiatric doctor overseeing Kristen’s care. Emily (Mamie Gummer): The rebellious patient. Sarah (Danielle Panabaker): The flirtatious ward member. Iris (Lyndsy Fonseca): The artistic one. Zoey (Laura-Leigh): The childlike ward resident. As the plot unfolds, Kristen encounters a menacing ghost that threatens her and the other patients. The screenplay by Michael and Shawn Rassmussen provides a basic horror framework, focusing primarily on the haunting atmosphere and character interactions. Cinematography and Direction Carpenter’s direction ensures that “The Ward,” while not exceptionally frightening, maintains momentum. His use of 35mm cinematography preserves its visual appeal, as viewers follow Kristen through the hospital’s dark corridors. Limited special effects allow Carpenter’s talent for composition to shine through, resulting in engaging visual storytelling. A Cast of Women Unlike many of Carpenter’s prior works, “The Ward” features a predominantly female cast. This shift offers a refreshing perspective within the horror genre. Amber Heard’s performance as Kristen adds depth to the character, navigating elements of slasher and noir styles. Reception and Cultural Context Upon its premiere at the Toronto Film Festival, “The Ward” struggled to find a significant audience during its commercial release in summer 2011. Released shortly after the theatrically mismanaged “Sucker Punch,” it received minimal attention, relegating it to a swift home-video distribution. Even with its lack of initial acclaim, “The Ward” stands as a confident entry in Carpenter’s later work. It serves as a thoughtful conclusion to his big-screen horror contributions, inviting viewers to explore themes of trauma and resilience. Now, horror fans have the opportunity to reclaim this overlooked film. Where to Watch “The Ward” is available for streaming on: Prime Video Peacock Tubi As audiences continue to discover John Carpenter’s underrated film, “The Ward,” it might finally achieve the recognition it deserves. The release date for the third season of the Gabriel Basso -led show hasn’t been revealed yet, now nearly a year after the second installment dropped ten new episodes that received a Certified Fresh rating of 86% on Rotten Tomatoes. What’s the new update for The Night Agent? According to Deadline, The Night Agent has scored a $31.6 million (40%) California tax credit, confirming the streamer’s plans to relocate the show’s main filming location from New York City to Los Angeles. This new update also appears to guarantee the show’s Season 4 renewal. Even though Netflix hasn’t officially greenlit Season 4, its writers’ room has already begun. Based on Matthew Quirk’s novel, The Night Agent was created and executive-produced by Shawn Ryan . The cast includes Gabriel Basso, Luciane Buchanan, Amanda Warren, Louis Herthum, Berto Colon, Michael Malarkey, Keon Alexander, Hong Chau, Arienne Mandi, Brittany Snow, Teddy Sears, Navid Negahban, and Rob Heaps. Season 3 will also introduce new characters played by Jennifer Morrison (Once Upon a Time), Stephen Moyer (True Blood), David Lyons (Revolution), Genesis Rodriguez (Lioness), Suraj Sharma (How I Met Your Father), and Callum Vinson (Chucky). “The series is a sophisticated, character-based, action-thriller centering on a low-level FBI Agent, Peter Sutherland, whose efforts to save The President in Season 1 earn him an opportunity to become a Night Agent in Season 2,” reads the show’s newest synopsis. “But working in the secretive organization of Night Action will propel Peter into a world where danger is everywhere and trust is in short supply.” (Source: Deadline ) Maggie Dela Paz Maggie Dela Paz has been writing about the movie and TV industry for more than seven years now. Besides being a fan of coming-of-age films and shows, she also enjoys watching K-Dramas and listening to her favorite K-Pop groups. Her current TV obsessions right now are FX’s The Bear and the popular anime My Hero Academia. In an interview, the actress responded to audience discussions and fan art imagining her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman. The conversation reignited interest in the DCU’s upcoming projects under Gunn’s “Gods and Monsters” chapter. Alexandra Daddario hasn’t seen any of her Wonder Woman fan art Alexandra Daddario recently addressed speculation about her potential involvement in James Gunn’s DC Universe during an interview with ScreenRant . While promoting her new film, I Wish You All The Best, Alexandra Daddario addressed fan art that depicts her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman, two roles audiences have imagined her playing in the new DCU. “I have to be honest, I haven’t seen any of that [fan art],” she said. She added, “I’m flattered to hear that it’s happening, but I haven’t seen it,” noting she wasn’t aware of the fan casting. When the interviewer asked if she would join Gunn’s DC Universe, Daddario replied, “Of course, working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn’t aware that that was going on.” Both Wonder Woman and Catwoman will appear in upcoming DCU projects. Gunn revealed on Threads on September 29, 2025, that Catwoman will appear in the franchise, though her specific project remains unannounced. Meanwhile, the Wonder Woman feature film entered early development in June 2025, with Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow writer Ana Nogueira set to pen the script. Additionally, a prequel series titled Paradise Lost remains in slow development. Gunn told Entertainment Weekly that it is “moving,” but the project does not yet have a finalized creative team. While fans continue to share casting theories, DC Studios has not announced any actors for its Wonder Woman reboot. If the script progresses as planned, industry speculation suggests a possible release window around 2028. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Mason Deaver\'s emotional novel I Wish You All The Best has made its way to the screen, and the team behind the film put all of their heart into faithfully translating the soul of their source material. The coming-of-age drama centers on Ben DeBacker, a high school senior who comes out to their parents as non-binary, but is swiftly thrown out of their home, turning to their estranged older sister, Hannah, for help. Hannah, along with her husband Thomas and their infant, take Ben in and set them up at the high school Thomas works at in order for them to finish their education. Despite their efforts to stay an anonymous entity among their classmates, Ben begins to grow close with Nathan, a charismatic classmate for whom they develop feelings, and Ms. Lyons, the school\'s art teacher who works to help Ben unlock their creativity and help them process their turbulent family situation. Tommy Dorfman, best known for her acting work in Netflix\'s 13 Reasons Why and The CW\'s Jane the Virgin , makes her feature directorial debut on I Wish You All The Best and has assembled a star-studded roster for it. My Life with the Walter Boys vet Corey Fogelmanis leads the ensemble as Ben, alongside Smile 2 \'s Miles Gutierrez-Riley as Nathan, Mayfair Witches \' Alexandra Daddario as Hannah, Riverdale \'s Cole Sprouse as Thomas and Girls \' Lena Dunham as Ms. Lyons. As the movie finally makes its way to theaters after its acclaimed South by Southwest 2024 debut, ScreenRant interviewed Tommy Dorfman, Corey Fogelmanis and Alexandra Daddario to discuss I Wish You All The Best . In looking particularly at the most important element of the novel Dorfman sought to adapt, the writer/director pointed to " the intimacy " of Deaver\'s source material , describing how reading the book fully immerses readers in Ben\'s story: Tommy Dorfman: It\'s written almost like a diary, at times, and that was one of the more challenging things, I think, to bring to screen is, how do we bring that internal experience that you get so vividly through Ben\'s perspective in a book, and give audiences an opportunity to kind of fly on the wall with them? Be with them over this very specific, concentrated six months of their life? Feeling " most protective " and " most precious " about exploring Ben\'s emotional rollercoasters, Dorfman found that once she had determined the best way to capture their inner struggles, " everything else came in through that perspective ", with the script then falling into place. Though denoting that " there were 20 versions of this script " before they finally started filming , the majority of that time was her " corseting ", " tightening " and getting the film to " the place of specificity that I think allows for universality and the best performances ". Corey Fogelmanis Had To Be "As Present As Possible" To Capture Ben\'s Ever-Changing Emotions ScreenRant: A question I have for you, Corey, is that so much of B\'s journey in I Wish You All The Best is internal. They go on such an emotional roller coaster ride throughout this film. What was it like for you as a performer, really ensuring that you\'re capturing every little nuance, whether it\'s a laugh that turns into a cry, like at the party, or just a genuine sense of finding oneself? Corey Fogelmanis: Yeah, I think for me, it was just so important that I was as present as possible. I\'d never had the experience of being in every scene of a movie before. So for me, I was just really focused on making sure that I was meeting everybody where they were at, and it kept my energy up. But I think, in a lot of ways, what we were filming kind of mirrored my experience on set. So I remember the first week being very disorienting, and that was when we were shooting the stuff of Ben coming to Hannah\'s house for the first time. I think I just really tried to trust where I was at, and Tommy did a really wonderful job of letting me know when it was working, and when it wasn\'t working, and helping me just keep track of everything. So, it was just kind of about trusting. ScreenRant: Alexandra talked a lot about trust, as well, when I just spoke with her, and I love that you were all able to form that trust with one another. That brings me to another question I have for you, Corey, which is that so much of B\'s story revolves around letting their walls down with Nathan and with Ms. Lyons. I know that this may get you in trouble with one of them, but I would love to hear if, between Lena and Miles, there was anybody whose connection you felt really carried over from off-camera into on-camera for your scenes together? Corey Fogelmanis\' Ben and Miles Gutierrez-Riley\'s Nathan laying on each other on a beach in I Wish You All The Best Corey Fogelmanis: I\'m gonna have to give this one to Miles, because we just had a lot more time together. We only had one day with Lena, and I wish it could have been the whole shoot, but I think when Miles came in, he found me on that first day, just kind of really grappling with having this whole world spinning around me, and he was so present, and really met me where I was at, and I really appreciated that. I think that was definitely the basis of Ben and Nathan\'s relationship, was that care off camera, and it was so spontaneous and wonderful, doing everything with Miles. Alexandra Daddario Got To Explore Her Maternal Instincts Through Her Character Alexandra Daddario\'s Hannah with her hand on Thomas\' chest and smiling at Ben in I Wish You All The Best ScreenRant: I want to talk about Hannah, because she is such a nicely layered character, in that she wants to be this great ally and strong sister, but also has a family that she\'s trying to raise. Looking at a scene, like after the party, when B comes home late, what is it like finding the balance between all of those layers playing this character throughout the film? Alexandra Daddario: I think it\'s just like being a mother. I hadn\'t had a child when we shot this yet, I have one now, and I think I was so on that track, and wanted to be a mother for so long that there was definitely that part of me. I think that\'s what being a mom is about. It\'s really about trying to find balance and staying calm and supporting people. Ultimately, when you have younger people in your life, they\'re going to be on their own paths, and be living their own lives. How do you help guide them, while also allowing them the freedom to go and be who they\'re going to be? That\'s what she\'s taking on, and it\'s a really beautiful job. ScreenRant: I love the way that really resonates in your and Corey\'s dynamic on screen. I\'d love to hear if that sort of protectiveness also carried over into off-camera, given Corey is still sort of on the rise of late, and you\'ve got some great experience working on everything from blockbusters to indies like this. Alexandra Daddario\'s Hannah looking sweetly with her hand on Ben\'s shoulder as they look at a necklace in I Wish You All The Best Alexandra Daddario: I think Corey is an incredibly impressive actor and will do great, great things. I was inspired, because I know how hard it is to be young and to be coming up. It\'s, again, a journey, it\'s something you have to go through and figure out on your own. The most important thing you can have is support from people. So, I was really impressed by Tommy\'s support, and how Tommy and Corey worked together. I think Corey is always going to have people who really, really care and are there to support. ScreenRant: One thing I love is that I Wish You All The Best premiered at South by Southwest back in \'24 and has just been getting rave reviews since. It\'s a little over a year since it made its premiere, but how has it been watching the reception over the course of the past year and a half for this film? Alexandra Daddario: I think it\'s wonderful. I\'m just a small part of the movie, and to be able to be part of it is incredible. But I think it\'s an important story to tell, and I\'m very, very happy that this movie exists, and that people are going to be able to see it. ScreenRant: Did you dive into the novel at all, by the way, for preparation when you were doing this film, or did you really just trust in Tommy? Alexandra Daddario: I did not, actually, this is the first time [I\'ve been asked], I\'m embarrassed to say I did not read the novel. But no, I really leaned on Tommy as a director, and her confidence. I felt I really understood the story and understood my character, and we just had a ton of fun. The set was as peaceful as could be. It really allowed all the actors to come together and do great work. So we had a really wonderful time. After weeks of fevered speculation, Hollywood star Alexandra Daddario has finally broken her silence on viral rumours linking her to the iconic superhero role in James Gunn's rebooted DC Universe. The White Lotus and Mayfair Witches actress has found herself at the heart of a global fan campaign after social media erupted with fancasts imagining her as the next Diana Prince. Fans across TikTok, X and Reddit have been flooding timelines with digital posters and fan art of Daddario in the Amazonian armour, convinced she is destined to inherit Gal Gadot's crown. But now, Daddario herself has spoken, and her answer may not be what fans were hoping for. How the Hype Began The frenzy began earlier this year when DC Studios boss James Gunn confirmed that Wonder Woman would return in future projects. Almost overnight, fancasts took over the internet, with thousands of fans declaring Daddario their top pick to wield the Lasso of Truth. Her cool, commanding presence and past work in action blockbusters made her an instant favourite, while tags such as #AlexandraDaddarioWonderWoman trended for days. Despite the excitement, DC Studios has yet to make any official casting announcements, keeping fans guessing and fuelling endless online debate. Daddario's Response Speaking to ScreenRant , Daddario addressed the viral speculation head-on, confirming that she has not been approached for the role. 'I have to be honest, I haven't seen any of that [fan art],' she said when asked about the buzz. She added that while she finds the attention flattering, there are no talks taking place. The actress also praised Gunn's creative direction, making clear that she would be open to working with him one day. 'But of course, working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn't aware that that was going on,' she added. Her calm and candid response may have cooled the current wave of hysteria, but it has also made fans even more determined to see her in the role. @hayabusa_i.a #cosplay #wonderwoman #dc #alexandradaddario ♬ sonido original - Jeff🧃 Gunn's New DC Vision Since taking over DC Studios in 2023, Gunn has been reshaping the superhero franchise under the banner Chapter One: Gods and Monsters . Confirmed titles include Superman: Legacy , The Brave and the Bold and an untitled Wonder Woman film currently in early development. Industry insiders say a writer originally attached to a Teen Titans project has now joined the Wonder Woman script team. Gunn later clarified that while the film is a priority, it is not being rushed, as the studio wants a strong story before production begins. Why Fans Think She Is the One Fans insist Daddario's mix of strength, grace and on-screen magnetism makes her the perfect fit for Wonder Woman. Her performances in San Andreas , Baywatch and Percy Jackson and the Olympians proved her action credentials, while The White Lotus showcased her emotional depth and charisma. Supporters argue that she embodies the balance of power and compassion that defines Diana Prince, a warrior with humanity. Even without confirmation, the idea of Daddario as Wonder Woman has taken on a life of its own, keeping her name at the centre of every fan wishlist. Life Beyond the Rumours Away from the speculation, Daddario continues to balance stardom with family life . She currently stars as Dr Rowan Fielding in AMC's Mayfair Witches , based on Anne Rice's gothic novels, and welcomed her first child in 2024 with husband Andrew Form, the producer behind A Quiet Place . While fans may still be dreaming of her in the red-and-gold armour, Daddario's poised response proves she does not need a tiara to shine. Hollywood already sees her as a queen in her own right. In an interview, the actress responded to audience discussions and fan art imagining her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman. The conversation reignited interest in the DCU’s upcoming projects under Gunn’s “Gods and Monsters” chapter. Alexandra Daddario hasn’t seen any of her Wonder Woman fan art Alexandra Daddario recently addressed speculation about her potential involvement in James Gunn’s DC Universe during an interview with ScreenRant . While promoting her new film, I Wish You All The Best, Alexandra Daddario addressed fan art that depicts her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman, two roles audiences have imagined her playing in the new DCU. “I have to be honest, I haven’t seen any of that [fan art],” she said. She added, “I’m flattered to hear that it’s happening, but I haven’t seen it,” noting she wasn’t aware of the fan casting. When the interviewer asked if she would join Gunn’s DC Universe, Daddario replied, “Of course, working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn’t aware that that was going on.” Both Wonder Woman and Catwoman will appear in upcoming DCU projects. Gunn revealed on Threads on September 29, 2025, that Catwoman will appear in the franchise, though her specific project remains unannounced. Meanwhile, the Wonder Woman feature film entered early development in June 2025, with Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow writer Ana Nogueira set to pen the script. Additionally, a prequel series titled Paradise Lost remains in slow development. Gunn told Entertainment Weekly that it is “moving,” but the project does not yet have a finalized creative team. While fans continue to share casting theories, DC Studios has not announced any actors for its Wonder Woman reboot. If the script progresses as planned, industry speculation suggests a possible release window around 2028. The coming-of-age drama centers on Ben DeBacker, a high school senior who comes out to their parents as non-binary, but is swiftly thrown out of their home, turning to their estranged older sister, Hannah, for help. Hannah, along with her husband Thomas and their infant, take Ben in and set them up at the high school Thomas works at in order for them to finish their education. Despite their efforts to stay an anonymous entity among their classmates, Ben begins to grow close with Nathan, a charismatic classmate for whom they develop feelings, and Ms. Lyons, the school\'s art teacher who works to help Ben unlock their creativity and help them process their turbulent family situation. Tommy Dorfman, best known for her acting work in Netflix\'s 13 Reasons Why and The CW\'s Jane the Virgin , makes her feature directorial debut on I Wish You All The Best and has assembled a star-studded roster for it. My Life with the Walter Boys vet Corey Fogelmanis leads the ensemble as Ben, alongside Smile 2 \'s Miles Gutierrez-Riley as Nathan, Mayfair Witches \' Alexandra Daddario as Hannah, Riverdale \'s Cole Sprouse as Thomas and Girls \' Lena Dunham as Ms. Lyons. As the movie finally makes its way to theaters after its acclaimed South by Southwest 2024 debut, ScreenRant interviewed Tommy Dorfman, Corey Fogelmanis and Alexandra Daddario to discuss I Wish You All The Best . In looking particularly at the most important element of the novel Dorfman sought to adapt, the writer/director pointed to " the intimacy " of Deaver\'s source material , describing how reading the book fully immerses readers in Ben\'s story: Tommy Dorfman: It\'s written almost like a diary, at times, and that was one of the more challenging things, I think, to bring to screen is, how do we bring that internal experience that you get so vividly through Ben\'s perspective in a book, and give audiences an opportunity to kind of fly on the wall with them? Be with them over this very specific, concentrated six months of their life? Feeling " most protective " and " most precious " about exploring Ben\'s emotional rollercoasters, Dorfman found that once she had determined the best way to capture their inner struggles, " everything else came in through that perspective ", with the script then falling into place. Though denoting that " there were 20 versions of this script " before they finally started filming , the majority of that time was her " corseting ", " tightening " and getting the film to " the place of specificity that I think allows for universality and the best performances ". Corey Fogelmanis Had To Be "As Present As Possible" To Capture Ben\'s Ever-Changing Emotions ScreenRant: A question I have for you, Corey, is that so much of B\'s journey in I Wish You All The Best is internal. They go on such an emotional roller coaster ride throughout this film. What was it like for you as a performer, really ensuring that you\'re capturing every little nuance, whether it\'s a laugh that turns into a cry, like at the party, or just a genuine sense of finding oneself? Corey Fogelmanis: Yeah, I think for me, it was just so important that I was as present as possible. I\'d never had the experience of being in every scene of a movie before. So for me, I was just really focused on making sure that I was meeting everybody where they were at, and it kept my energy up. But I think, in a lot of ways, what we were filming kind of mirrored my experience on set. So I remember the first week being very disorienting, and that was when we were shooting the stuff of Ben coming to Hannah\'s house for the first time. I think I just really tried to trust where I was at, and Tommy did a really wonderful job of letting me know when it was working, and when it wasn\'t working, and helping me just keep track of everything. So, it was just kind of about trusting. ScreenRant: Alexandra talked a lot about trust, as well, when I just spoke with her, and I love that you were all able to form that trust with one another. That brings me to another question I have for you, Corey, which is that so much of B\'s story revolves around letting their walls down with Nathan and with Ms. Lyons. I know that this may get you in trouble with one of them, but I would love to hear if, between Lena and Miles, there was anybody whose connection you felt really carried over from off-camera into on-camera for your scenes together? Corey Fogelmanis\' Ben and Miles Gutierrez-Riley\'s Nathan laying on each other on a beach in I Wish You All The Best Corey Fogelmanis: I\'m gonna have to give this one to Miles, because we just had a lot more time together. We only had one day with Lena, and I wish it could have been the whole shoot, but I think when Miles came in, he found me on that first day, just kind of really grappling with having this whole world spinning around me, and he was so present, and really met me where I was at, and I really appreciated that. I think that was definitely the basis of Ben and Nathan\'s relationship, was that care off camera, and it was so spontaneous and wonderful, doing everything with Miles. Alexandra Daddario Got To Explore Her Maternal Instincts Through Her Character Alexandra Daddario\'s Hannah with her hand on Thomas\' chest and smiling at Ben in I Wish You All The Best ScreenRant: I want to talk about Hannah, because she is such a nicely layered character, in that she wants to be this great ally and strong sister, but also has a family that she\'s trying to raise. Looking at a scene, like after the party, when B comes home late, what is it like finding the balance between all of those layers playing this character throughout the film? Alexandra Daddario: I think it\'s just like being a mother. I hadn\'t had a child when we shot this yet, I have one now, and I think I was so on that track, and wanted to be a mother for so long that there was definitely that part of me. I think that\'s what being a mom is about. It\'s really about trying to find balance and staying calm and supporting people. Ultimately, when you have younger people in your life, they\'re going to be on their own paths, and be living their own lives. How do you help guide them, while also allowing them the freedom to go and be who they\'re going to be? That\'s what she\'s taking on, and it\'s a really beautiful job. The actress says she was 'flattered but unaware' of the viral fancasting By Michael Toledo Published 02 November 2025, 9:49 AM GMT Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket Alexandra Daddario Alexandra Daddario/Instagram Is she or isn't she the next Wonder Woman? After weeks of fevered speculation, Hollywood star Alexandra Daddario has finally broken her silence on viral rumours linking her to the iconic superhero role in James Gunn's rebooted DC Universe. The White Lotus and Mayfair Witches actress has found herself at the heart of a global fan campaign after social media erupted with fancasts imagining her as the next Diana Prince. Fans across TikTok, X and Reddit have been flooding timelines with digital posters and fan art of Daddario in the Amazonian armour, convinced she is destined to inherit Gal Gadot's crown. But now, Daddario herself has spoken, and her answer may not be what fans were hoping for. How the Hype Began The frenzy began earlier this year when DC Studios boss James Gunn confirmed that Wonder Woman would return in future projects. Almost overnight, fancasts took over the internet, with thousands of fans declaring Daddario their top pick to wield the Lasso of Truth. Her cool, commanding presence and past work in action blockbusters made her an instant favourite, while tags such as #AlexandraDaddarioWonderWoman trended for days. Despite the excitement, DC Studios has yet to make any official casting announcements, keeping fans guessing and fuelling endless online debate. Daddario's Response Speaking to ScreenRant , Daddario addressed the viral speculation head-on, confirming that she has not been approached for the role. 'I have to be honest, I haven't seen any of that [fan art],' she said when asked about the buzz. She added that while she finds the attention flattering, there are no talks taking place. The actress also praised Gunn's creative direction, making clear that she would be open to working with him one day. 'But of course, working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn't aware that that was going on,' she added. Her calm and candid response may have cooled the current wave of hysteria, but it has also made fans even more determined to see her in the role. @hayabusa_i.a #cosplay #wonderwoman #dc #alexandradaddario ♬ sonido original - Jeff🧃 Gunn's New DC Vision Since taking over DC Studios in 2023, Gunn has been reshaping the superhero franchise under the banner Chapter One: Gods and Monsters . Confirmed titles include Superman: Legacy , The Brave and the Bold and an untitled Wonder Woman film currently in early development. Industry insiders say a writer originally attached to a Teen Titans project has now joined the Wonder Woman script team. Gunn later clarified that while the film is a priority, it is not being rushed, as the studio wants a strong story before production begins. Why Fans Think She Is the One Fans insist Daddario's mix of strength, grace and on-screen magnetism makes her the perfect fit for Wonder Woman. Her performances in San Andreas , Baywatch and Percy Jackson and the Olympians proved her action credentials, while The White Lotus showcased her emotional depth and charisma. Supporters argue that she embodies the balance of power and compassion that defines Diana Prince, a warrior with humanity. Even without confirmation, the idea of Daddario as Wonder Woman has taken on a life of its own, keeping her name at the centre of every fan wishlist. Life Beyond the Rumours Away from the speculation, Daddario continues to balance stardom with family life . She currently stars as Dr Rowan Fielding in AMC's Mayfair Witches , based on Anne Rice's gothic novels, and welcomed her first child in 2024 with husband Andrew Form, the producer behind A Quiet Place . While fans may still be dreaming of her in the red-and-gold armour, Daddario's poised response proves she does not need a tiara to shine. Hollywood already sees her as a queen in her own right. It seems Emily Blunt is still taking style notes from her iconic The Devil Wears Prada days! She knows how to deliver a fashion moment, and her arrival at the 16th Governors Awards reminded everyone of just that. On Sunday afternoon, as she graced the Hollywood red carpet in a red gown, all eyes were on her. Emily Blunt channelled the confidence of someone who once survived Miranda Priestly’s icy glare, as she slipped into a Schiaparelli gown for the evening. Fresh off the runway Pic courtesy: X/ @ebbrphotos Emily Blunt, who played Emily, Miranda Priestly’s assistant in The Devil Wears Prada , the ultimate fashion bible, knows a thing or two about fashion. Ruling the runway is practically her forte. For the Sunday evening, she wore a red gown from Schiaparelli’s Ready-to-Wear Spring/Summer 2026 collection. Designed by Daniel Roseberry, the satin floor-length gown was a perfect marriage of haute couture artistry and red-carpet glamour — the best of both worlds. Staying true to Schiaparelli's legendary surrealist aesthetic, the gown featured an extraordinary sculptural element on one shoulder that resembled a rosette in full bloom. The double-faced satin dress was embellished with tulle inserts, creating cut-outs on either side of the hips. Emily has never been afraid of taking fashion risks, and this time was no different. She carried a coordinating red leather clutch to maintain the monochromatic vision from head to toe. The teardrop diamond from Messika added just the right amount of sparkle. She tied her hair into a middle-parted bun and opted for a fresh make-up look. Emily Blunt looked absolutely stunning in the red gown. The glittery red carpet Emily Blunt walked the red carpet by herself. Her husband, fellow actor John Krasinski, was notably absent from the festivities. The A Quiet Place director is currently in New York City filming Jack Ryan , the highly anticipated film continuation of his beloved political action thriller series. Meanwhile, Emily Blunt also met her The Smashing Machine co-star Dwayne Johnson on the red carpet. The event also saw some of the A-listers from the industry, including Ariana Grande, Lucy Liu, Jeremy Strong, Leonardo DiCaprio, Michael B. Jordan, Mia Goth and Oscar Isaac, among others. Emily Blunt calls The Devil Wears Prada ‘terribly moving’, describes the sequel as a ‘delicious experience’ Emily Blunt reflects on her emotional return to 'The Devil Wears Prada 2', highlighting how the original film transformed her career and remains a source of comfort for audiences. She praises its evolution from satire to deeper themes and its empowering message for women. Trisha Bhattacharya Published 13 Nov 2025, 06:54 PM IST Emily Blunt in the behind-the-scenes from 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' (LEFT) and as Emily Charlton in the 2006-film 'The Devil Wears Prada' (RIGHT). ( Getty Images / 20th Century Studios ) Nearly two decades after 'The Devil Wears Prada' became a global phenomenon, Emily Blunt has opened up about reprising her role in the long-awaited sequel, calling the experience deeply emotional. Emily Blunt on reprising the role of Emily Charlton in 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' The Academy award nominated British actor reflected on the film that changed her life, her early days in Hollywood, and why the 2006 hit continues to resonate with audiences today. “It’s terribly moving,” she said in a recent interview about stepping back into her iconic role. “Because it changed everything. David Frankel [the director] changed my life by casting me when I was an unknown. I’d been working, but no one knew who I was, and he was so sure that he wanted me in the movie, from a taped reading. That meant a huge amount to me.” Also Read | Meryl Streep's ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ officially begins production Blunt, who will reprise her fan-favourite character in ' The Devil Wears Prada 2 '—set to release next year—reflected on how the original role opened new creative paths for her. “Emily was such a ludicrous character,” she acknowledged, “but in the best way. It did leave the door open for people to see me as more than a British period drama girl. It paved the way for character roles, which is all I wanted. I didn’t want to be an ingenue. I was curious to explore an entire bag of tricks.” Did Emily Blunt reveal details from the much-awaited sequel? Though the actor remained tight-lipped about details of the sequel, she spoke with warmth about the film’s enduring legacy. “The movie now is like a nostalgia bank for people,” Blunt said. “People have watched that movie 50 times. They’ve watched it with a sick parent; they’ve watched it when they go through a breakup. It has been a source of comfort and escapism. And the movie is really incredible as well. I think it’s a beautiful movie.” She praised the film’s evolution from satire to something far more meaningful. “In many ways, what starts off as a comedy—with the shock factor of the things they say, how they say them, and the ruthless nature of the fashion industry—then turns into something much more poignant and deep. I think it’s that shift in tone that people really gravitate toward.” Blunt also commended the creative team for crafting a story that transcends its glamorous setting. “What David Frankel and [screenwriter] Aline Brosh McKenna did with the script is really clever. That’s a really hard needle to thread in a world that could be deemed superficial, to create such depth in characters. [It also tackles] our understanding of ambition, what it looks like, what it means, what the fallouts are, what the undoing is.” Emily Blunt on 'The Devil Wears Prada' being a franchise that stands for women empowerment She added that ' The Devil Wears Prada ' remains a powerful and empowering story for women. “It’s a really empowering movie for women as well. Miranda Priestly’s character, if she were male, which the movie touches on, would have been deemed impressive rather than the nicknames that she was on the receiving end of. And I also get why people have really just salivated over all the one-liners; it’s so quotable. It’s delicious. It’s a delicious experience and I get it.” Blunt’s return to the world of high fashion and razor-sharp wit promises to bring the same charm and insight that made the original a timeless classic — one that continues to inspire, comfort, and delight audiences nearly twenty years on. The Rock is a Hollywood star who needs little introduction, and the wrestler-turned-actor has been a box office juggernaut for decades. However, he\'s also been pigeonholed into certain roles. The sports biopic , The Smashing Machine , was supposed to be Johnson\'s pivot towards dramatic parts, but that didn\'t work out. The film was a box office disaster, grossing $30 million less than its reported production budget (via Box Office Mojo ). While it might have been a cathartic experience for Johnson, the flop says a lot about the actor\'s career. Why The Rock’s Dramatic Role Failed & Others Didn’t Dwayne Johnson as Mark Kerr sitting on a gym floor in The Smashing Machine The Rock isn\'t the first actor to try something different, and plenty of typecast stars have broken out in more dramatic or comedic parts . Jim Carrey famously starred in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind and gave an all-time classic performance. However, what sets The Rock apart is the passage of time, and The Smashing Machine just came too late. When Carrey made his dramatic turn, he was a decade into his movie star career. Fans had grown accustomed to his humor, but it certainly wasn\'t overdone. On the other hand, The Rock has been a generic action star for nearly 25 years, with little variation . If The Smashing Machine was made 10 years ago, the story might be different. In an era of increasingly volatile box offices , The Smashing Machine was already behind the eight-ball. The movie had nothing to appeal to Johnson\'s fans , while more artistically-inclined cinephiles were likely turned off by the presence of an action star in a drama. This was shown in the financial numbers, and the movie fell into limbo. It was no secret that The Smashing Machine was The Rock\'s dramatic turn, but that wasn\'t enough to get audience to flock to theaters. Since the entire movie hinged on Johnson\'s dramatic performance, its rejection is proof that moviegoers just didn\'t want to see it after two-and-a-half decades of safe Rock fare. It\'s important to note that the failure of The Rock\'s dramatic turn isn\'t dependent on the quality of his performance. In fact, Johnson showed just how strong his acting skills have become when playing Mark Kerr. The effusive praise that Johnson received for his performance was not misplaced , and he showed the skills he possessed all along. The Smashing Machine Wasn’t Different Enough Mark Kerr walks down the aisle to the ring in The Smashing Machine Another reason that The Rock\'s dramatic turn failed was that there was no element of surprise . The marketing for the film made it clear that Rocky was not playing his usual character, so audiences got the whole story before they even saw the movie. On top of that, The Rock playing an MMA fighter was just too close to reality. The Rock\'s time as a wrestler was beloved, and he\'s maintained the aura of a larger-than-life superstar ever since. Therefore, a role involving combat sports wasn\'t all that unique . Had The Rock played a character wholly unlike himself, it could have been better recieved. The Smashing Machine was familiar, which was its ultimate downfall. 6.5 /10 4 /10 The Smashing Machine 10 stars 9 stars 8 stars 7 stars 6 stars 5 stars 4 stars 3 stars 2 stars 1 star Like Follow Followed R Drama History Release Date October 3, 2025 Runtime 123 minutes Director Benny Safdie 5 Images Dwayne Johnson & Emily Blunt in The Smashing Machine The Rock as Mark Kerr wearing a white hat and sitting down in The Smashing Machine Dwayne Johnson in a hospital bed in The Smashing Machine. The Oscar-winning actors are reprising their antagonistic roles for The Devil Wears Prada 2 which is set for release next summer. ‘The age of toys is over’: first Toy Story 5 teaser trailer introduces a new tech foe Read more Streep, who was Oscar-nominated for her role of tyrannical magazine editor Miranda Priestly in the original, has not appeared in a film since 2021’s Don’t Look Up. She also recently signed on to star next to Sigourney Weaver in thriller Useful Idiots. The pair will be joined by returning cast members Emily Blunt and Stanley Tucci with Kenneth Branagh joining the cast as Priestly’s new husband. The film will also feature Simone Ashley, Rachel Bloom and Lucy Liu and reported cameos from Lady Gaga and Sydney Sweeney. The sequel, again directed by David Frankel, will see Priestly dealing with the collapse of the magazine industry, now forced to build bridges with her one-time assistant Emily (Blunt) who is the head of a luxury brand and its advertising spend. The original 2006 comedy, based on the novel by Lauren Weisberger, made over $326m at the global box office. It later spawned a West End musical. “When we made the first movie, none of us expected the meteoric life that it would have and the impact it would have on people,” Blunt said back in September . She added that it also “has deep emotional roots” for her and Tucci who later became her brother-in-law. Priestly has been widely perceived to be inspired by Anna Wintour, the former editor-in-chief of Vogue. Wintour recently spoke about the original film and Streep’s performance, saying it “had a lot of humour to it. It had a lot of wit. It had Meryl Streep. I mean, it was Emily Blunt , [and] they were all amazing. In the end, I thought it was a fair shot”. The shoot has attracted the attention of photographers and fans across the globe with locations ranging from Brooklyn to Milan. The film also marks a major year for Hathaway who will also appear opposite Michaela Coel in David Lowery’s pop star drama Mother Mary, a film with original music from Charli xcx. The year will also see her star in Colleen Hoover adaptation Verity with Dakota Johnson, sci-fi thriller Flowervale Street with Ewan McGregor and Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey alongside Tom Holland and Zendaya. The Devil Wears Prada 2 will be released in a summer filled with sequels including Scary Movie 6, Toy Story 5, Minions 3 and Spider-Man: Brand New Day. This article was amended on 12 November 2025. In an earlier version, Anna Wintour had been incorrectly referred to as the outgoing rather than former editor-in-chief of Vogue. By: Entertainment Desk November 13, 2025 09:25 AM IST 3 min read Whatsapp twitter Facebook Reddit PRINT Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway return with The Devil Wears Prada 2 after 20 years. Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway are all set to return to the screen with the highly anticipated The Devil Wears Prada 2, and fans just got a glimpse of their iconic collaboration. The makers of the film have unveiled the teaser along with Meryl and Anne’s first looks. The teaser begins with a visual of a woman walking in red stilettos through an office. As people rush to get out of her way, we soon realise that the woman in the video is none other than Meryl Streep, reprising her role as the formidable Runway magazine editor-in-chief, Miranda Priestly, from the original 2006 film. While everyone hurriedly steps aside, a hand stops the elevator, where Miranda is standing alone. Enter her former assistant, Andy Sachs, played by Anne Hathaway, who joins her just in time. This prompts Miranda to say, “Took you long enough,” making Andy smirk and slip on her black sunglasses. Andy getting into the same elevator as Miranda also hints that the dynamic between them has evolved and they are now more like equals. A sequel? For spring? Groundbreaking. Meryl Streep, Anne Hathaway, Emily Blunt, and Stanley Tucci return in The Devil Wears Prada 2, in theaters May 1, 2026. Watch the teaser trailer now. pic.twitter.com/QzcIn4f6G0 — 20th Century Studios (@20thcentury) November 12, 2025 The teaser was shared by 20th Century Studios, who wrote, “A sequel? For spring? Groundbreaking. Meryl Streep, Anne Hathaway, Emily Blunt, and Stanley Tucci return in The Devil Wears Prada 2, in theaters May 1, 2026. Watch the teaser trailer now.” Fans have been going gaga over the teaser and the sight of Anne and Meryl reuniting. A fan wrote, “No words for how excited I am to have these icons back!” Another fan observed, “The fact that Miranda actually moves to the side to give Andy more room is some major character development.” Another fan added, “The absence of Blunt from this teaser somehow makes me even more excited to see how she’ll be in this sequel.” Emily Blunt, who played Miranda’s other assistant in the original film, is also confirmed to be part of the sequel. Stanley Tucci is also returning to the film. The Devil Wears Prada 2 will revolve around Miranda’s career as she tries to navigate a world where print journalism is dying. The film is directed by David Frankel, who also helmed the original. Lady Gaga, Kenneth Branagh, Lucy Liu, Justin Theroux, B.J. Novak, Pauline Chalamet, and Simone Ashley will also be seen in the new film. Expand Click for more updates and latest Hollywood News along with Bollywood and Entertainment updates . It seems Emily Blunt is still taking style notes from her iconic The Devil Wears Prada days! She knows how to deliver a fashion moment, and her arrival at the 16th Governors Awards reminded everyone of just that. On Sunday afternoon, as she graced the Hollywood red carpet in a red gown, all eyes were on her. Emily Blunt channelled the confidence of someone who once survived Miranda Priestly’s icy glare, as she slipped into a Schiaparelli gown for the evening. Fresh off the runway Pic courtesy: X/ @ebbrphotos Emily Blunt, who played Emily, Miranda Priestly’s assistant in The Devil Wears Prada , the ultimate fashion bible, knows a thing or two about fashion. Ruling the runway is practically her forte. For the Sunday evening, she wore a red gown from Schiaparelli’s Ready-to-Wear Spring/Summer 2026 collection. Designed by Daniel Roseberry, the satin floor-length gown was a perfect marriage of haute couture artistry and red-carpet glamour — the best of both worlds. Staying true to Schiaparelli's legendary surrealist aesthetic, the gown featured an extraordinary sculptural element on one shoulder that resembled a rosette in full bloom. The double-faced satin dress was embellished with tulle inserts, creating cut-outs on either side of the hips. Emily has never been afraid of taking fashion risks, and this time was no different. She carried a coordinating red leather clutch to maintain the monochromatic vision from head to toe. The teardrop diamond from Messika added just the right amount of sparkle. She tied her hair into a middle-parted bun and opted for a fresh make-up look. Emily Blunt looked absolutely stunning in the red gown. The glittery red carpet Emily Blunt walked the red carpet by herself. Her husband, fellow actor John Krasinski, was notably absent from the festivities. The A Quiet Place director is currently in New York City filming Jack Ryan , the highly anticipated film continuation of his beloved political action thriller series. Meanwhile, Emily Blunt also met her The Smashing Machine co-star Dwayne Johnson on the red carpet. The event also saw some of the A-listers from the industry, including Ariana Grande, Lucy Liu, Jeremy Strong, Leonardo DiCaprio, Michael B. Jordan, Mia Goth and Oscar Isaac, among others. Emily Blunt calls The Devil Wears Prada ‘terribly moving’, describes the sequel as a ‘delicious experience’ Emily Blunt reflects on her emotional return to 'The Devil Wears Prada 2', highlighting how the original film transformed her career and remains a source of comfort for audiences. She praises its evolution from satire to deeper themes and its empowering message for women. Trisha Bhattacharya Published 13 Nov 2025, 06:54 PM IST Emily Blunt in the behind-the-scenes from 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' (LEFT) and as Emily Charlton in the 2006-film 'The Devil Wears Prada' (RIGHT). ( Getty Images / 20th Century Studios ) Nearly two decades after 'The Devil Wears Prada' became a global phenomenon, Emily Blunt has opened up about reprising her role in the long-awaited sequel, calling the experience deeply emotional. Emily Blunt on reprising the role of Emily Charlton in 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' The Academy award nominated British actor reflected on the film that changed her life, her early days in Hollywood, and why the 2006 hit continues to resonate with audiences today. “It’s terribly moving,” she said in a recent interview about stepping back into her iconic role. “Because it changed everything. David Frankel [the director] changed my life by casting me when I was an unknown. I’d been working, but no one knew who I was, and he was so sure that he wanted me in the movie, from a taped reading. That meant a huge amount to me.” Also Read | Meryl Streep's ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ officially begins production Blunt, who will reprise her fan-favourite character in ' The Devil Wears Prada 2 '—set to release next year—reflected on how the original role opened new creative paths for her. “Emily was such a ludicrous character,” she acknowledged, “but in the best way. It did leave the door open for people to see me as more than a British period drama girl. It paved the way for character roles, which is all I wanted. I didn’t want to be an ingenue. I was curious to explore an entire bag of tricks.” Did Emily Blunt reveal details from the much-awaited sequel? Though the actor remained tight-lipped about details of the sequel, she spoke with warmth about the film’s enduring legacy. “The movie now is like a nostalgia bank for people,” Blunt said. “People have watched that movie 50 times. They’ve watched it with a sick parent; they’ve watched it when they go through a breakup. It has been a source of comfort and escapism. And the movie is really incredible as well. I think it’s a beautiful movie.” She praised the film’s evolution from satire to something far more meaningful. “In many ways, what starts off as a comedy—with the shock factor of the things they say, how they say them, and the ruthless nature of the fashion industry—then turns into something much more poignant and deep. I think it’s that shift in tone that people really gravitate toward.” Blunt also commended the creative team for crafting a story that transcends its glamorous setting. “What David Frankel and [screenwriter] Aline Brosh McKenna did with the script is really clever. That’s a really hard needle to thread in a world that could be deemed superficial, to create such depth in characters. [It also tackles] our understanding of ambition, what it looks like, what it means, what the fallouts are, what the undoing is.” Emily Blunt on 'The Devil Wears Prada' being a franchise that stands for women empowerment She added that ' The Devil Wears Prada ' remains a powerful and empowering story for women. “It’s a really empowering movie for women as well. Miranda Priestly’s character, if she were male, which the movie touches on, would have been deemed impressive rather than the nicknames that she was on the receiving end of. And I also get why people have really just salivated over all the one-liners; it’s so quotable. It’s delicious. It’s a delicious experience and I get it.” Blunt’s return to the world of high fashion and razor-sharp wit promises to bring the same charm and insight that made the original a timeless classic — one that continues to inspire, comfort, and delight audiences nearly twenty years on.
