The results of the long-awaited dramatic turn speak for themselves. Johnson\'s Oscar-buzzy feature The Smashing Machine debuted at film festivals to a positive reception, with his performance in particular heralded. The Smashing Machine Is Now On Digital After Disappointing Theatrical Debut Dwayne Johnson as Mark Kerr sitting on a gym floor in The Smashing Machine A24 originally released The Smashing Machine in theaters on October 3 with the hopes that the wide release would spark plenty of awards discussions but also allow the $50 million production to turn a profit with a star like Johnson front and center . That is not what happened. Audiences have liked the film overall, but not enough people are going to a theater to watch it. The disappointing theatrical reception is why A24 released The Smashing Machine on digital today, November 4 . It\'s currently available on PVOD services like Amazon and Fandango. Anyone who is a fan of Dwayne Johnson or curious about what a dramatic performance from him is really like should absolutely check out The Smashing Machine . There\'s also a rather effective true story told about real-life fighter Mark Kerr , whom Johnson transformed physically and emotionally to bring to life. This could wind up being a turning point for The Rock\'s career, as he has continued to seek out more challenging film roles after. The Rock is a Hollywood star who needs little introduction, and the wrestler-turned-actor has been a box office juggernaut for decades. However, he\'s also been pigeonholed into certain roles. The sports biopic , The Smashing Machine , was supposed to be Johnson\'s pivot towards dramatic parts, but that didn\'t work out. The film was a box office disaster, grossing $30 million less than its reported production budget (via Box Office Mojo ). While it might have been a cathartic experience for Johnson, the flop says a lot about the actor\'s career. Why The Rock’s Dramatic Role Failed & Others Didn’t Dwayne Johnson as Mark Kerr sitting on a gym floor in The Smashing Machine The Rock isn\'t the first actor to try something different, and plenty of typecast stars have broken out in more dramatic or comedic parts . Jim Carrey famously starred in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind and gave an all-time classic performance. However, what sets The Rock apart is the passage of time, and The Smashing Machine just came too late. When Carrey made his dramatic turn, he was a decade into his movie star career. Fans had grown accustomed to his humor, but it certainly wasn\'t overdone. On the other hand, The Rock has been a generic action star for nearly 25 years, with little variation . If The Smashing Machine was made 10 years ago, the story might be different. In an era of increasingly volatile box offices , The Smashing Machine was already behind the eight-ball. The movie had nothing to appeal to Johnson\'s fans , while more artistically-inclined cinephiles were likely turned off by the presence of an action star in a drama. This was shown in the financial numbers, and the movie fell into limbo. It was no secret that The Smashing Machine was The Rock\'s dramatic turn, but that wasn\'t enough to get audience to flock to theaters. Since the entire movie hinged on Johnson\'s dramatic performance, its rejection is proof that moviegoers just didn\'t want to see it after two-and-a-half decades of safe Rock fare. It\'s important to note that the failure of The Rock\'s dramatic turn isn\'t dependent on the quality of his performance. In fact, Johnson showed just how strong his acting skills have become when playing Mark Kerr. The effusive praise that Johnson received for his performance was not misplaced , and he showed the skills he possessed all along. The Smashing Machine Wasn’t Different Enough Mark Kerr walks down the aisle to the ring in The Smashing Machine Another reason that The Rock\'s dramatic turn failed was that there was no element of surprise . The marketing for the film made it clear that Rocky was not playing his usual character, so audiences got the whole story before they even saw the movie. On top of that, The Rock playing an MMA fighter was just too close to reality. The Rock\'s time as a wrestler was beloved, and he\'s maintained the aura of a larger-than-life superstar ever since. Therefore, a role involving combat sports wasn\'t all that unique . Had The Rock played a character wholly unlike himself, it could have been better recieved. The Smashing Machine was familiar, which was its ultimate downfall. 6.5 /10 4 /10 The Smashing Machine 10 stars 9 stars 8 stars 7 stars 6 stars 5 stars 4 stars 3 stars 2 stars 1 star Like Follow Followed R Drama History Release Date October 3, 2025 Runtime 123 minutes Director Benny Safdie 5 Images Dwayne Johnson & Emily Blunt in The Smashing Machine The Rock as Mark Kerr wearing a white hat and sitting down in The Smashing Machine Dwayne Johnson in a hospital bed in The Smashing Machine. By Shaun Kitchener Published: 21 November 2025 There\'s bad news for anyone awaiting the sequel to 2021 flick Jungle Cruise , as stars Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt have revealed it is no longer on the cards - at least for now. The film was released just as cinemas reopened after COVID lockdowns, and was enough of a success to warrant quick plans for a follow-up. Now, however, it seems those plans have sunk. Speaking to Entertainment Weekly as they promote their new team-up The Smashing Machine , Johnson and Blunt were asked if Jungle Cruise 2 is still en route, to which they are both quoted as replying: "I don\'t think so." What to Read Next Johnson explained: "I think when Disney came under new leadership, they just shifted coming out of COVID. COVID shifted our business in a lot of ways. "I think they looked at that property and thought, we did it once, not sure if we should revisit it again. Despite whether or not our chemistry was great." Frank Masi // Disney Related: Best film and TV tours for 2025 Blunt quipped that bosses "did not want to set sail again, and that\'s fine." Johnson had previously expressed huge excitement at the prospect of revisiting their characters, tweeting back in 2021: "ALL ABOARD... This is going to be FUN!" The film also starred Édgar Ramírez, Jesse Plemmons, Paul Giamatti and a much-discussed Jack Whitehall , with direction from Jaume Collet-Serra. The Smashing Machine , meanwhile, is a very different affair, and stars Johnson as former amateur wrestler and MMA fighter Mark Kerr, with Blunt as his girlfriend Dawn Staples. A24 Related: Best streaming services It has a solid 70% approval score on Rotten Tomatoes , with the consensus saying: "Dwayne Johnson goes the distance with his transformative turn as Mark Kerr in The Smashing Machine , a gritty biopic that sidesteps cliché even at the expense of narrative satisfaction while still landing the dramatic body blows that count." It had a successful premiere at the Venice International Film Festival back in September, where Johnson burst into tears and writer-director Benny Safdie won the Silver Lion. Blunt will soon be back in comedy territory in the long-awaited sequel The Devil Wears Prada 2 , which is due in May 2026 and released its teaser trailer - with a first glimpse of Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway - earlier this month. The makers of the film have unveiled the teaser along with Meryl and Anne’s first looks. The teaser begins with a visual of a woman walking in red stilettos through an office. It marks her fourth time working with director Yorgos Lanthimos and her third time in as many years. Bugonia had the biggest wide-opening weekend for a Yorgos Lanthimos movie , which proves that both audiences and critics alike are enjoying the film. As is often the case with Lanthimos, Bugonia has already won over critics, amassing an 86% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. This is particularly a welcome change after Stone and Lanthimos\' previous movie, Kinds of Kindness , which was divisive for audiences, although it did find some success on streaming. Bugonia has received more universal love from moviegoers, and rightfully so. As a "Good For Her" movie, Bugonia gives viewers the one thing KInds of Kindness fails to do , which explains why the same audience loves Bugonia much more. Both films have a twisted sense of humor, but only Kinds of Kindness was co-written by the director, unlike Bugonia , which was written by Will Tracy, based on Save the Green Planet! Emma Stone\'s Characters in Kinds Of Kindness Are Punching Bags Emma Stone extending a fork to feed her husband in Kinds of Kindness Kinds of Kindness is an anthology of three chapters that are connected by their themes. They all explore the violent, terrifying, and depraved depths that humanity descends into when it succumbs to cynicism. The movie\'s lack of joy is disappointing, as you are emotionally exhausted by the time the first chapter ends, making the next two feel like a task. Emma Stone only has a minor role in the first chapter, but she is a supporting character in the second one, and the protagonist in the third. In chapter two, "R.M.F Is Flying" , she plays Liz, a marine biologist who inexplicably returns after disappearing during an expedition. She is different from when she left and even her shoes don\'t fit. Her husband, Daniel (Jesse Plemons), becomes increasingly erratic and orders her to mutilate herself for his enjoyment, eating her finger at one point, and eventually her liver, causing her death. It is also suggested that he\'s responsible for having beaten her and caused her miscarriage . In the third chapter, "R.M.F. Eats A Sandwich" , Emma Stone plays a cultist named Emily. Emily and her husband belong to a cult based on sexual purity and loyalty. After she is raped by her estranged husband, who drugs her after inviting her over to spend time with her estranged daughter, she is unfairly kicked out of the cult. Her desperate attempt to rejoin the cult brutally fails in the ending of Kinds of Kindness . Kinds of Kindness Has No Proper Emotional Release Emma Stone in Kinds of Kindness The biggest flaw in Kinds of Kindness is that builds up emotional frustration without giving viewers any release. The conclusion is decidedly cynical and depressing. Emma Stone\'s characters in the second and third chapters suffer endlessly without getting escape or revenge, and you root for her in vain, eventually annoyed by the lack of satisfaction that the stories give you. We see her suffer the consequences of being raped, and that doesn\'t sit right with me. Emily\'s a victim in the movie, and watching her accidentally kill the only person who could help her rejoin the cult is aggravating. It\'s only worsened by realizing her solution was trying to return to the same cult that vilified her for being raped . Bugonia Gives Emma Stone\'s Character A Satisfying Ending Michelle Fuller (Emma Stone) smiling at her corporate office in Bugonia ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection In Bugonia , Emma Stone plays Michelle Fuller, a corporate CEO, who is kidnapped by two men, Teddy (Jesse Plemons) and Don (Aidan Delbis), because the former believes she\'s an alien. They shave her head, imprison her in their basement, and Teddy tortures her. She denies his claims, but Bugonia \'s ending, which is more obvious than shocking , confirms he was right. However, the film doesn\'t favor him. He may have successfully predicted that she was an alien, but he only arrived at the conclusion after torturing and killing many other people for evidence and information about Andromedans. Bugonia ensures we know he is an evil person, even if he is proven right. You root for Emma Stone\'s character throughout Bugonia \'s runtime. But here\'s how Bugonia improves on Kinds of Kindness \'s fatal flaw – Emma Stone\'s Michelle Fuller gets the last laugh in the movie . She eventually uses Teddy\'s conviction to manipulate him into freeing her, and then uses her freedom to kill him. All the resentment for Teddy that you feel growing inside you is paid off in Bugonia \'s satisfying climax. Bugonia\'s Ending Feels Happy and Deserved As Lanthimos, Stone, and Plemons have explained, Bugonia \'s ending isn\'t a sad one despite the annihilation of all human life at Michelle\'s hands. After she ascends to the mothership and kills every human being on Earth, you still feel a sense of contentment that she escaped Teddy\'s clutches and made the only natural decision she could after her traumatizing experience. As Michelle tells Teddy in the climax, Andromedans had been kind enough to repopulate the Earth with species resembling them after they accidentally caused the dinosaurs\' extinction. However, Teddy\'s behavior is symptomatic of humanity\'s cynicism. He chooses not to engage in more open-minded ways instead of torturing her, and earns humanity its extinction in what feels like a happy ending. Dakota Johnson , the star from the film ‘Materialists’, recently moderated an interview between the main cast of ‘Bugonia’ as well as its director, Yorgos Lanthimos . While talking about the film, the actress ended up joking about how Lanthimos should consider other actresses for his roles, making everyone laugh. Read on to know what else happened at the interview. Dakota Johnson jokes that Yorgos Lanthimos should consider other actresses besides Emma Stone As per The Hollywood Reporter, Dakota Johnson played the role of the moderator between Emma Stone, Yorgos Lanthimos, and Jesse Plemons, the cast of ‘Bugonia’ at their special screening at CAA. While talking to the cast about the film, the actress admitted that she had seen it already and had loved it. Chris Martin Arrives In Mumbai With Dakota Johnson For Coldplay's India Gig | WATCH Moving forward, however, she also ended up joking about how Yorgos Lanthimos only likes to work with Emma Stone. ‘Bugonia’ is their 4th film together, including ‘Kinds of Kindness’, ‘The Favourite’, and ‘Poor Things’, as well. She talked to the famed director about the matter, joking that, “Are you aware that there are other actresses, that are really talented, maybe even very close by?”, hinting at her own self. Stone then enthusiastically encouraged Johnson to give her pitch to the director while laughing, to which the ‘Fifty Shades’ actress replied by saying, “I already did and it didn’t work, remember? You were there,” making everyone laugh out loud. Emma Stone on her role in the film The actress delved into her experience of portraying the character of a CEO who has been kidnapped by a couple of theorists who think that she is an alien. She added on that, “I had never played a character that I thought about the audience seeing it for the second time before. Would it still make sense? Would it be able to track through if you were watching the film again, knowing what you know — like I did after reading the script for the first time — and have more to give or be interesting in some way? There are great cinematic team-ups that audiences look forward to, with actors squaring off on screen. Robert De Niro and Al Pacino in Heat , Colin Firth and Hugh Grant in Bridget Jones Diary , and even Arnold Schwarzenegger and Sylvester Stallone in The Expendables . But what project could unite Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone after all these years? None other than a Miss Piggy movie. Yes, Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone are going to appear in a Muppet movie. Speaking with Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers’ Las Culturistas podcast (via Deadline ), Lawrence revealed that she and Stone are working together on a Miss Piggy film with Oh, Mary! playwright and star Cole Escola penning the script. "I don’t know if I can announce this, but I’m just going to. Emma Stone and I are producing a Miss Piggy movie, and Cole is writing it." When asked if she or Stone would star in the film, Lawrence said, "I think so, we have to." Jennifer Lawrence & Emma Stone Are a Team-Up Years in the Making Jennifer Lawrence in American Hustle Sony Pictures Releasing Emma Stone and Jennifer Lawrence are considered two of the greatest actors of their generation, both of whom loomed large in the 2010s thanks to a mix of franchise work and awards contenders. Lawrence won the Best Actress Oscar for Silver Linings Playbook , with Stone winning her first Best Actress Academy Award in La La Land, before winning her second for Poor Things . In the 2010s, both were also stars of some iconic film franchises. Lawrence played Mystique in the X-Men prequel films and Katniss Everdeen in The Hunger Games , while Stone played Gwen Stacy in The Amazing Spider-Man films. Between them, their resumes include beloved titles like American Hustle, Birdman or (An Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance), Winter\'s Bone, The Favourite, Joy, and Easy A , to name a few. Both are also in the Oscar race this year, Stone for her performance in Bugonia and Lawrence for Lynn Ramsey\'s Die My Love . It feels like a collaboration that has been years in the making, and Miss Piggy seems to be the perfect vehicle for it. Miss Piggy made her debut in 1974 in Herb Alpert and the TJB before becoming one of the leads of The Muppet Show , and she quickly became one of the group\'s most iconic figures. Often known for her diva star persona, Miss Piggy is quick to anger and has been known to throw down. She tends to flirt with the guest stars of The Muppet Show , but the love of her life remains Kermit the Frog. Miss Piggy herself is an icon, with TV Guide ranking her number 23 on its 50 Greatest TV Stars of All Time list in 1996. In 1979, two Cincinnati Muppet fans even launched a campaign to get Miss Piggy nominated for a Best Actress Oscar for her role in The Muppet Movie . The Miss Piggy solo film by Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone is the latest high-profile Muppet project to come from Disney in the past few months. In September, it was reported that Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg were filming a Muppet Show special for Disney+ to air in 2026 in honor of the series\' 50th anniversary. The special will star Sabrina Carpenter , and if it is a hit, it could be the backdoor pilot for a new series. After years of fans expressing frustration with how Disney has handled and ignored The Muppets, it appears that some of the biggest names in Hollywood are showing their love for the characters known by pitching, producing, and starring in titles that audiences can\'t help but take notice of. Palash Muchhal Dharmendra Natasa Stankovic Hema Malini Ameesha Patel Happy Birthday Emma Stone: From La La Land to Bugonia, a look at her most iconic roles Hollywood star Emma Stone still slaying with her charm, wit, and killer comic timing. From Easy A to La La Land and Cruella, here’s a look at her most iconic and unforgettable roles that cemented her as a true Hollywood powerhouse. Curated by : Gayatri Rani November 06, 2025 / 06:01 IST 1/10 Hollywood actress Emma Stone is celebrating her 37th birthday on November 6, 2025. The actress continues to captivate audiences with her charm, adaptability, and flawless comedic timing. From her breakthrough performance in Easy A to her Oscar-winning performance in Damien Chazelle's La La Land, she made a name for herself in the film industry. Take a look at some of her iconic roles over the years. 2/10 La La Land Damien Chazelle's 2016 musical romance La La Land, which starred Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling, is about an aspiring actress, Mia, who works as a barista while she waits for her big break, and a struggling musician, Sebastian, who is compelled to play the piano in cover bands and restaurants from the 1980s. The two start dating and end up falling in love. But as Mia and Sebastian encounter a turning point in their relationship and careers, they realise that success has a cost. The bagged six Oscars out of 14 nominations and is still one of the best romances of the 21st century. 3/10 Poor Things Emma Stone stars in this provocative black comedy about a female Frankenstein coming of age, in her second feature film with Lanthimos. Following her tragic suicide, Dr Godwin Baxter (Willem Dafoe) resurrects Bella Baxter (Stone), a young woman. Despite being an adult, Bella behaves like a child because Dr. Baxter gave her an infant's brain. Bella experiences a sexual and intellectual awakening as she makes her way in the world and spends more time in it. The actress delivered an exceptional performance. 4/10 Crazy, Stupid, Love This 2011 rom-com revolves around Steve Carell's character, Cal Weaver, who is completely upended when his wife Emily (Julianne Moore) requests a divorce following an affair with a coworker. As a coping mechanism, a lost Cal begins going to a local bar and talking to women about his wife. Jacob Palmer (Ryan Gosling), a womaniser, notices Cal's despair and takes him under his wing, teaching him how to woo women. Jacob gradually realises that he only wants to win the heart of one girl, Hannah (Emma Stone), as Cal succeeds with other women. Advertisement Remove Ad Advertisement Remove Ad 5/10 Easy A Speaking of romantic comedies, Easy A is unquestionably a tribute to all of the greatest romantic films from the 1980s. An intelligent high school student named Olive (Emma Stone) unintentionally persuades the entire school that she will sleep with anyone in exchange for money. The film explores romance, agency, and choice. Additionally, Emma Stone and Penn Badgley's amazing chemistry won over the fans. 6/10 The Help Emma plays aspiring author Skeeter Phelan in this film, who collaborates with the African American maids in Jackson, Mississippi, in 1963 to share their experiences. In addition to learning about it herself, Skeeter illuminates the daily injustices and discrimination these women encounter. 7/10 The Amazing Spider-Man In Marc Webb's action epic, Emma plays the role of whip-smart, honey-blond Gwen Stacy, the first love of Andrew Garfield's web-slinging Peter Parker. She brought the franchise back to life with her trademark sardonic charm. She reappeared for The Amazing Spider-Man 2 two years later. However, the death of Gwen Stacy is still one of the heartbreaking scenes in the franchise. 8/10 Bugonia The most recent work by Emma and Lanthimos is a black comedy remake of Save the Green Planet!, a 2003 South Korean film. She portrays Michelle Fuller, the CEO of a pharmaceutical company, who is abducted by Teddy (Jesse Plemons), a conspiracy theorist who thinks Michelle is part of an invading alien race that is in charge of the human race. Advertisement Remove Ad Advertisement Remove Ad 9/10 Kinds of Kindness Emma Stone's third film with Lanthimos, Kinds of Kindness, is a cinematic triptych that consists of three distinct stories, each in which Emma and the rest of the cast (including Margaret Qualley, Joe Alwyn, Willem Dafoe, and Jesse Plemons) play distinct characters. The unusual format allowed Stone to flex her acting abilities. 10/10 Cruella In Craig Gillespie's supervillain origin story, Emma portrays the role of glitzy, giggling Cruella de Vil, exposing the resilient, punk rock underdog who came before her. An orphan who turns to stealing out of need, she aspires to be a fashion designer and, when offered the opportunity by a cold couturier (Emma Thompson), finds that she has the secret to her tragic past. On the whole, Bugonia is different, mind bending and treat for cinephiles. (Todd Owyoung/NBC) Jennifer Lawrence is sharing new details about the Miss Piggy film she is developing with Emma Stone . The actress revealed what originally sparked the idea for the movie centered on the iconic Muppet, which Cole Escola is writing, in a recent appearance on The Tonight Show . “So, during lockdown, one of my good friends who is not in the industry—it was also kind of around cancel culture, it was like both things were kind of happening at once. After setting up the backstory, Lawrence described how the premise was derived. “Miss Piggy is a feminist icon, and she said it would be so funny if Miss Piggy got canceled. Now, that is not the plot, necessarily, but it got the wheels turning,” Lawrence said. The actress also noted that “there hasn’t actually been” a solo film centered around Miss Piggy before. “I started kind of producing it. But Emma Stone is the Muppet-head. Focus Features Bugonia , director Yorgos Lanthimos’ latest film with Emma Stone, is new in theaters. When will it be available to watch at home? Bugonia came out in limited release on Oct. 24 and expands to theaters nationwide on Friday. The logline for Bugonia reads, “Two conspiracy-obsessed young men kidnap the high-powered CEO of a major company, convinced that she is an alien intent on destroying planet Earth.” Forbes ‘Bugonia’ Rotten Tomatoes Reviews: Is Emma Stone’s Film Alienating Critics? By Tim Lammers The film also stars Jesse Plemons , Aidan Delbis, Stavros Halkias and Alicia Silverstone. Currently, the only way you can see Bugonia is in theaters, so check your local listings for showtimes. When Bugonia comes to the home entertainment marketplace, its first stop will be on digital streaming via premium video on demand. Typically, it takes Focus Features’ releases anywhere from 18 days to a month from the time they open wide in theaters to the time they arrive on PVOD. Jennifer Lawrence reveals Miss Piggy movie plans 6 November 2025 Share Save Naomi Clarke BBC Newsbeat Share Save Getty Images Miss Piggy has become a pop culture fixture over the years Miss Piggy is set to finally get her solo movie moment, with Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone on board for the new project. Lawrence revealed she will co-produce the film, centered on the diva puppet from The Muppets franchise, alongside close friend Stone. Speaking on the Las Culturistas podcast, she said: "I don\'t know if I can announce this but I\'m just gonna. Emma Stone and I are producing a Miss Piggy movie." She also said US actor and playwright Cole Escola, who starred in the award-winning Broadway comedy Oh, Mary!, was writing the script. Getty Images Jennifer Lawrence has never been in a movie with Emma Stone Lawrence says she thinks the Miss Piggy film could be the first time she co-stars with Stone. "It\'s like really dark that we haven\'t done a movie together," she added. Lawrence shared more details about the project during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on Wednesday evening. She said she\'d discussed the idea with a friend during the pandemic lockdown and how it would be "so funny" if Miss Piggy was cancelled. The actress stressed that was "not the plot necessarily" but it "got the wheels turning" about a starring role for the character, hailing her as a "feminist icon". Lawrence also revealed that Stone was the "Muppet head" out of the two, while she branded herself as the "ideas guy". Getty Images Miss Piggy is known for her on-and-off-again relationship with The Muppet\'s lead character, Kermit the Frog Miss Piggy started off as a background character on The Muppet Show back in the mid-1970s. But she soon began to steal the limelight on the TV series with her sassy personality and glamorous looks. She is also known for her on-and-off-again relationship with The Muppet\'s lead character, Kermit the Frog, and has appeared alongside him in several films. The Muppet Show, which celebrates its 50th anniversary next year, is due to air a one-off special featuring US pop star Sabrina Carpenter. Disney announced the return of fan-favourite characters "to the Muppet Theatre to put on a variety show filled with music, comedy, and plenty of chaos". It marks her fourth time working with director Yorgos Lanthimos and her third time in as many years. Bugonia had the biggest wide-opening weekend for a Yorgos Lanthimos movie , which proves that both audiences and critics alike are enjoying the film. As is often the case with Lanthimos, Bugonia has already won over critics, amassing an 86% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. This is particularly a welcome change after Stone and Lanthimos\' previous movie, Kinds of Kindness , which was divisive for audiences, although it did find some success on streaming. Bugonia has received more universal love from moviegoers, and rightfully so. As a "Good For Her" movie, Bugonia gives viewers the one thing KInds of Kindness fails to do , which explains why the same audience loves Bugonia much more. Both films have a twisted sense of humor, but only Kinds of Kindness was co-written by the director, unlike Bugonia , which was written by Will Tracy, based on Save the Green Planet! Emma Stone\'s Characters in Kinds Of Kindness Are Punching Bags Emma Stone extending a fork to feed her husband in Kinds of Kindness Kinds of Kindness is an anthology of three chapters that are connected by their themes. They all explore the violent, terrifying, and depraved depths that humanity descends into when it succumbs to cynicism. The movie\'s lack of joy is disappointing, as you are emotionally exhausted by the time the first chapter ends, making the next two feel like a task. Emma Stone only has a minor role in the first chapter, but she is a supporting character in the second one, and the protagonist in the third. In chapter two, "R.M.F Is Flying" , she plays Liz, a marine biologist who inexplicably returns after disappearing during an expedition. She is different from when she left and even her shoes don\'t fit. Her husband, Daniel (Jesse Plemons), becomes increasingly erratic and orders her to mutilate herself for his enjoyment, eating her finger at one point, and eventually her liver, causing her death. It is also suggested that he\'s responsible for having beaten her and caused her miscarriage . In the third chapter, "R.M.F. Eats A Sandwich" , Emma Stone plays a cultist named Emily. Emily and her husband belong to a cult based on sexual purity and loyalty. After she is raped by her estranged husband, who drugs her after inviting her over to spend time with her estranged daughter, she is unfairly kicked out of the cult. Her desperate attempt to rejoin the cult brutally fails in the ending of Kinds of Kindness . Kinds of Kindness Has No Proper Emotional Release Emma Stone in Kinds of Kindness The biggest flaw in Kinds of Kindness is that builds up emotional frustration without giving viewers any release. The conclusion is decidedly cynical and depressing. Emma Stone\'s characters in the second and third chapters suffer endlessly without getting escape or revenge, and you root for her in vain, eventually annoyed by the lack of satisfaction that the stories give you. We see her suffer the consequences of being raped, and that doesn\'t sit right with me. Emily\'s a victim in the movie, and watching her accidentally kill the only person who could help her rejoin the cult is aggravating. It\'s only worsened by realizing her solution was trying to return to the same cult that vilified her for being raped . Bugonia Gives Emma Stone\'s Character A Satisfying Ending Michelle Fuller (Emma Stone) smiling at her corporate office in Bugonia ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection In Bugonia , Emma Stone plays Michelle Fuller, a corporate CEO, who is kidnapped by two men, Teddy (Jesse Plemons) and Don (Aidan Delbis), because the former believes she\'s an alien. They shave her head, imprison her in their basement, and Teddy tortures her. She denies his claims, but Bugonia \'s ending, which is more obvious than shocking , confirms he was right. However, the film doesn\'t favor him. He may have successfully predicted that she was an alien, but he only arrived at the conclusion after torturing and killing many other people for evidence and information about Andromedans. Bugonia ensures we know he is an evil person, even if he is proven right. You root for Emma Stone\'s character throughout Bugonia \'s runtime. But here\'s how Bugonia improves on Kinds of Kindness \'s fatal flaw – Emma Stone\'s Michelle Fuller gets the last laugh in the movie . She eventually uses Teddy\'s conviction to manipulate him into freeing her, and then uses her freedom to kill him. All the resentment for Teddy that you feel growing inside you is paid off in Bugonia \'s satisfying climax. Bugonia\'s Ending Feels Happy and Deserved As Lanthimos, Stone, and Plemons have explained, Bugonia \'s ending isn\'t a sad one despite the annihilation of all human life at Michelle\'s hands. After she ascends to the mothership and kills every human being on Earth, you still feel a sense of contentment that she escaped Teddy\'s clutches and made the only natural decision she could after her traumatizing experience. As Michelle tells Teddy in the climax, Andromedans had been kind enough to repopulate the Earth with species resembling them after they accidentally caused the dinosaurs\' extinction. However, Teddy\'s behavior is symptomatic of humanity\'s cynicism. He chooses not to engage in more open-minded ways instead of torturing her, and earns humanity its extinction in what feels like a happy ending. Dakota Johnson , the star from the film ‘Materialists’, recently moderated an interview between the main cast of ‘Bugonia’ as well as its director, Yorgos Lanthimos . While talking about the film, the actress ended up joking about how Lanthimos should consider other actresses for his roles, making everyone laugh. Read on to know what else happened at the interview. Dakota Johnson jokes that Yorgos Lanthimos should consider other actresses besides Emma Stone As per The Hollywood Reporter, Dakota Johnson played the role of the moderator between Emma Stone, Yorgos Lanthimos, and Jesse Plemons, the cast of ‘Bugonia’ at their special screening at CAA. While talking to the cast about the film, the actress admitted that she had seen it already and had loved it. Chris Martin Arrives In Mumbai With Dakota Johnson For Coldplay's India Gig | WATCH Moving forward, however, she also ended up joking about how Yorgos Lanthimos only likes to work with Emma Stone. ‘Bugonia’ is their 4th film together, including ‘Kinds of Kindness’, ‘The Favourite’, and ‘Poor Things’, as well. She talked to the famed director about the matter, joking that, “Are you aware that there are other actresses, that are really talented, maybe even very close by?”, hinting at her own self. Stone then enthusiastically encouraged Johnson to give her pitch to the director while laughing, to which the ‘Fifty Shades’ actress replied by saying, “I already did and it didn’t work, remember? You were there,” making everyone laugh out loud. Emma Stone on her role in the film The actress delved into her experience of portraying the character of a CEO who has been kidnapped by a couple of theorists who think that she is an alien. She added on that, “I had never played a character that I thought about the audience seeing it for the second time before. Would it still make sense? Would it be able to track through if you were watching the film again, knowing what you know — like I did after reading the script for the first time — and have more to give or be interesting in some way? There are great cinematic team-ups that audiences look forward to, with actors squaring off on screen. Robert De Niro and Al Pacino in Heat , Colin Firth and Hugh Grant in Bridget Jones Diary , and even Arnold Schwarzenegger and Sylvester Stallone in The Expendables . But what project could unite Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone after all these years? None other than a Miss Piggy movie. Yes, Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone are going to appear in a Muppet movie. Speaking with Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers’ Las Culturistas podcast (via Deadline ), Lawrence revealed that she and Stone are working together on a Miss Piggy film with Oh, Mary! playwright and star Cole Escola penning the script. "I don’t know if I can announce this, but I’m just going to. Emma Stone and I are producing a Miss Piggy movie, and Cole is writing it." When asked if she or Stone would star in the film, Lawrence said, "I think so, we have to." Jennifer Lawrence & Emma Stone Are a Team-Up Years in the Making Jennifer Lawrence in American Hustle Sony Pictures Releasing Emma Stone and Jennifer Lawrence are considered two of the greatest actors of their generation, both of whom loomed large in the 2010s thanks to a mix of franchise work and awards contenders. Lawrence won the Best Actress Oscar for Silver Linings Playbook , with Stone winning her first Best Actress Academy Award in La La Land, before winning her second for Poor Things . In the 2010s, both were also stars of some iconic film franchises. Lawrence played Mystique in the X-Men prequel films and Katniss Everdeen in The Hunger Games , while Stone played Gwen Stacy in The Amazing Spider-Man films. Between them, their resumes include beloved titles like American Hustle, Birdman or (An Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance), Winter\'s Bone, The Favourite, Joy, and Easy A , to name a few. Both are also in the Oscar race this year, Stone for her performance in Bugonia and Lawrence for Lynn Ramsey\'s Die My Love . It feels like a collaboration that has been years in the making, and Miss Piggy seems to be the perfect vehicle for it. Miss Piggy made her debut in 1974 in Herb Alpert and the TJB before becoming one of the leads of The Muppet Show , and she quickly became one of the group\'s most iconic figures. Often known for her diva star persona, Miss Piggy is quick to anger and has been known to throw down. She tends to flirt with the guest stars of The Muppet Show , but the love of her life remains Kermit the Frog. Miss Piggy herself is an icon, with TV Guide ranking her number 23 on its 50 Greatest TV Stars of All Time list in 1996. In 1979, two Cincinnati Muppet fans even launched a campaign to get Miss Piggy nominated for a Best Actress Oscar for her role in The Muppet Movie . The Miss Piggy solo film by Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone is the latest high-profile Muppet project to come from Disney in the past few months. In September, it was reported that Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg were filming a Muppet Show special for Disney+ to air in 2026 in honor of the series\' 50th anniversary. The special will star Sabrina Carpenter , and if it is a hit, it could be the backdoor pilot for a new series. After years of fans expressing frustration with how Disney has handled and ignored The Muppets, it appears that some of the biggest names in Hollywood are showing their love for the characters known by pitching, producing, and starring in titles that audiences can\'t help but take notice of. Palash Muchhal Dharmendra Natasa Stankovic Hema Malini Ameesha Patel Happy Birthday Emma Stone: From La La Land to Bugonia, a look at her most iconic roles Hollywood star Emma Stone still slaying with her charm, wit, and killer comic timing. From Easy A to La La Land and Cruella, here’s a look at her most iconic and unforgettable roles that cemented her as a true Hollywood powerhouse. Curated by : Gayatri Rani November 06, 2025 / 06:01 IST 1/10 Hollywood actress Emma Stone is celebrating her 37th birthday on November 6, 2025. The actress continues to captivate audiences with her charm, adaptability, and flawless comedic timing. From her breakthrough performance in Easy A to her Oscar-winning performance in Damien Chazelle's La La Land, she made a name for herself in the film industry. Take a look at some of her iconic roles over the years. 2/10 La La Land Damien Chazelle's 2016 musical romance La La Land, which starred Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling, is about an aspiring actress, Mia, who works as a barista while she waits for her big break, and a struggling musician, Sebastian, who is compelled to play the piano in cover bands and restaurants from the 1980s. The two start dating and end up falling in love. But as Mia and Sebastian encounter a turning point in their relationship and careers, they realise that success has a cost. The bagged six Oscars out of 14 nominations and is still one of the best romances of the 21st century. 3/10 Poor Things Emma Stone stars in this provocative black comedy about a female Frankenstein coming of age, in her second feature film with Lanthimos. Following her tragic suicide, Dr Godwin Baxter (Willem Dafoe) resurrects Bella Baxter (Stone), a young woman. Despite being an adult, Bella behaves like a child because Dr. Baxter gave her an infant's brain. Bella experiences a sexual and intellectual awakening as she makes her way in the world and spends more time in it. The actress delivered an exceptional performance. 4/10 Crazy, Stupid, Love This 2011 rom-com revolves around Steve Carell's character, Cal Weaver, who is completely upended when his wife Emily (Julianne Moore) requests a divorce following an affair with a coworker. As a coping mechanism, a lost Cal begins going to a local bar and talking to women about his wife. Jacob Palmer (Ryan Gosling), a womaniser, notices Cal's despair and takes him under his wing, teaching him how to woo women. Jacob gradually realises that he only wants to win the heart of one girl, Hannah (Emma Stone), as Cal succeeds with other women. Advertisement Remove Ad Advertisement Remove Ad 5/10 Easy A Speaking of romantic comedies, Easy A is unquestionably a tribute to all of the greatest romantic films from the 1980s. An intelligent high school student named Olive (Emma Stone) unintentionally persuades the entire school that she will sleep with anyone in exchange for money. The film explores romance, agency, and choice. Additionally, Emma Stone and Penn Badgley's amazing chemistry won over the fans. 6/10 The Help Emma plays aspiring author Skeeter Phelan in this film, who collaborates with the African American maids in Jackson, Mississippi, in 1963 to share their experiences. In addition to learning about it herself, Skeeter illuminates the daily injustices and discrimination these women encounter. 7/10 The Amazing Spider-Man In Marc Webb's action epic, Emma plays the role of whip-smart, honey-blond Gwen Stacy, the first love of Andrew Garfield's web-slinging Peter Parker. She brought the franchise back to life with her trademark sardonic charm. She reappeared for The Amazing Spider-Man 2 two years later. However, the death of Gwen Stacy is still one of the heartbreaking scenes in the franchise. 8/10 Bugonia The most recent work by Emma and Lanthimos is a black comedy remake of Save the Green Planet!, a 2003 South Korean film. She portrays Michelle Fuller, the CEO of a pharmaceutical company, who is abducted by Teddy (Jesse Plemons), a conspiracy theorist who thinks Michelle is part of an invading alien race that is in charge of the human race. Advertisement Remove Ad Advertisement Remove Ad 9/10 Kinds of Kindness Emma Stone's third film with Lanthimos, Kinds of Kindness, is a cinematic triptych that consists of three distinct stories, each in which Emma and the rest of the cast (including Margaret Qualley, Joe Alwyn, Willem Dafoe, and Jesse Plemons) play distinct characters. The unusual format allowed Stone to flex her acting abilities. 10/10 Cruella In Craig Gillespie's supervillain origin story, Emma portrays the role of glitzy, giggling Cruella de Vil, exposing the resilient, punk rock underdog who came before her. An orphan who turns to stealing out of need, she aspires to be a fashion designer and, when offered the opportunity by a cold couturier (Emma Thompson), finds that she has the secret to her tragic past. On the whole, Bugonia is different, mind bending and treat for cinephiles. (Todd Owyoung/NBC) Jennifer Lawrence is sharing new details about the Miss Piggy film she is developing with Emma Stone . The actress revealed what originally sparked the idea for the movie centered on the iconic Muppet, which Cole Escola is writing, in a recent appearance on The Tonight Show . “So, during lockdown, one of my good friends who is not in the industry—it was also kind of around cancel culture, it was like both things were kind of happening at once. After setting up the backstory, Lawrence described how the premise was derived. “Miss Piggy is a feminist icon, and she said it would be so funny if Miss Piggy got canceled. Now, that is not the plot, necessarily, but it got the wheels turning,” Lawrence said. The actress also noted that “there hasn’t actually been” a solo film centered around Miss Piggy before. “I started kind of producing it. But Emma Stone is the Muppet-head. Focus Features Bugonia , director Yorgos Lanthimos’ latest film with Emma Stone, is new in theaters. When will it be available to watch at home? Bugonia came out in limited release on Oct. 24 and expands to theaters nationwide on Friday. The logline for Bugonia reads, “Two conspiracy-obsessed young men kidnap the high-powered CEO of a major company, convinced that she is an alien intent on destroying planet Earth.” Forbes ‘Bugonia’ Rotten Tomatoes Reviews: Is Emma Stone’s Film Alienating Critics? By Tim Lammers The film also stars Jesse Plemons , Aidan Delbis, Stavros Halkias and Alicia Silverstone. Currently, the only way you can see Bugonia is in theaters, so check your local listings for showtimes. When Bugonia comes to the home entertainment marketplace, its first stop will be on digital streaming via premium video on demand. Typically, it takes Focus Features’ releases anywhere from 18 days to a month from the time they open wide in theaters to the time they arrive on PVOD. Jennifer Lawrence reveals Miss Piggy movie plans 6 November 2025 Share Save Naomi Clarke BBC Newsbeat Share Save Getty Images Miss Piggy has become a pop culture fixture over the years Miss Piggy is set to finally get her solo movie moment, with Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone on board for the new project. Lawrence revealed she will co-produce the film, centered on the diva puppet from The Muppets franchise, alongside close friend Stone. Speaking on the Las Culturistas podcast, she said: "I don\'t know if I can announce this but I\'m just gonna. Emma Stone and I are producing a Miss Piggy movie." She also said US actor and playwright Cole Escola, who starred in the award-winning Broadway comedy Oh, Mary!, was writing the script. Getty Images Jennifer Lawrence has never been in a movie with Emma Stone Lawrence says she thinks the Miss Piggy film could be the first time she co-stars with Stone. "It\'s like really dark that we haven\'t done a movie together," she added. Lawrence shared more details about the project during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on Wednesday evening. She said she\'d discussed the idea with a friend during the pandemic lockdown and how it would be "so funny" if Miss Piggy was cancelled. The actress stressed that was "not the plot necessarily" but it "got the wheels turning" about a starring role for the character, hailing her as a "feminist icon". Lawrence also revealed that Stone was the "Muppet head" out of the two, while she branded herself as the "ideas guy". It\'s relaxing to spend an hour or more watching a predictable romance unfold or witnessing a character go on a transformative journey before it is time to unwrap gifts. Netflix \'s latest offering, Champagne Problems , meets the aforementioned criteria, plus the add-on benefit of stunning scenery. In it, Minka Kelly plays an ambitious executive who heads to Paris in the hopes of securing a lucrative deal with a long-standing champagne brand. As is common for most holiday titles, the protagonist goes on a business trip only to find a handsome and conveniently available French man to show her the city. With a European backdrop, romance between the leads, and champagne to spare (filling up a champagne glass while watching this would be fitting), this Netflix rom-com is poised to not only bring the jolly spirit back to full force but satisfy a craving for travel for those unable to plan a getaway abroad. What Is \'Champagne Problems\' About? When Sydney Price (Kelly) is faced with a major career opportunity, she takes it without hesitation. Yet, while she prepares to take off to Paris with a clear goal in mind, she makes a promise to her sister that she will at least take one night off from her trip to do some sightseeing and ultimately rediscover who she is and what she wants beyond her job. Despite being driven by the prospect of acquiring Château Cassell, a beloved French champagne house, she does free up her itinerary to pay a visit to a local bookstore, where she meets Henri Cassell ( Tom Wozniczka ). As expected, sparks fly instantly, with Sydney being drawn to him the more they spend time together, having some macaroons and hot chocolate while admiring the Eiffel Tower at night. Yet, to the protagonist\'s surprise, Henri is the son of Hugo Cassell ( Thibault de Montalembert ), the very person she came to Paris to negotiate with. As Sydney spends the weekend with Hugo, Henri, and other bidders, she is not only one step closer to making the acquisition happen, but becoming even more emotionally attached to the people she is with and the places she visits . \'Champagne Problems\' Feels Like a Scenic Getaway Tom Wozniczka and Minka Kelly in Champagne Problems Image via Netflix Champagne Problems might fit the bill for rom-com lovers seeking their next holiday watch , but it will also appeal to those who are on the lookout for their next holiday escape . Filmed in Paris, as well as Épernay and Reims, the film feels like a stunning venture into the places that Sydney visits throughout it, making viewers feel like they are just as much part of the experience. The main character has been so focused on making it professionally, that she has never gotten to travel for fun. As much as she travels to France for work, she gets to finally do something for her own enjoyment, and open herself to the prospect of love. Although the film does focus on her and Henri, Champagne Problems also features a mismatched group of buyers competing with Sydney to acquire Château Cassell. Amongst them are party animal Roberto Salazar ( Sean Amsing ), German misfit Otto Moller ( Flula Borg ), and the hostile-yet-driven Brigitte Laurent ( Astrid Whettnall ). Each of their different personalities dictate the ways in which they try to convince Hugo to sell his champagne empire, and it\'s entertaining to see their persuasion tactics put into motion. Although the supporting characters are primarily one-dimensional and stereotypical, their presence doesn\'t hinder the fun viewers have while watching them bond and go head-to-head in this civilized bidding war . Minka Kelly Is a Winning Christmas Rom-Com Lead in \'Champagne Problems\' Yet, without a doubt, Champagne Problems \' greatest asset is Minka Kelly. The Friday Night Lights alum, who recently graced the screen on Netflix\'s Ransom Canyon , proves to be a romantic lead worth rooting for . She isn\'t the typical iteration of the businesswoman we see in rom-coms like this. She might be passionate about her job, but she isn\'t the type of person looking to pick a fight in order to get what she wants. Throughout the film, Sydney lets go of her planner-oriented mindset and gives into the experience, not only becoming friends with Roberto, but also finding the love of her life. Kelly and Wozniczka, who many might know from Slow Horses , have just the right amount of chemistry to keep you invested. Their stroll through the Christmas market earlier in the film and their sweet exchange at the bookstore towards the end are the highlights of their romantic storyline. Although the couple do not share as much time on screen together as one would hope, writer-director Mark Steven Johnson made the right call in focusing on Sydney\'s path to self-discovery. As Hallmark-esque as this Netflix rom-com might be , it offers the perfect combo for what you anticipate from a seasonal title . It delivers on a low-stakes love story between two people from different cultural backgrounds, allows for its main character to grow into her own and understand her worth, and gives viewers the opportunity to escape to Paris without leaving their couch. Its supporting cast might not get the opportunity to go beyond their stereotypical constructs and the main pair might not get as many swoon-worthy sequences together as many might\'ve desired, but the film is able to check off all the boxes you would hope for. But more importantly, it makes a case for Kelly to join Kat Graham and Lindsay Lohan as part of the roster of romantic leads in Netflix holiday rom-coms. If this was her first foray into the Christmas movie pipeline, the hope is that it is certainly not her last. Champagne Problems is now available to stream on Netflix. Titans , which premiered on DC Universe in 2018 (and is now available on HBO Max), adapted the Teen Titans mythology and added an edge. The series followed Dick Grayson ( Brenton Thwaites ) as he emerged from Batman\'s death and created the next generation of heroes, including Starfire ( Anna Diop ), Raven ( Teagan Croft ), and Beast Boy ( Ryan Potter ). Ritchson was introduced into the series as Hank Hall, better known as Hawk — a battered, brutish hand-to-hand fighting vigilante who, along with Dove ( Minka Kelly ), brought street-level brutality and raw emotion to a series frequently teetering between superhero visuals and down-to-earth drama. For viewers who know Ritchson as the taciturn, near-superhuman Jack Reacher, Titans is the final piece of the puzzle that shows how long he has been capable of being the leading man of a franchise. What To Know About Alan Ritchson\'s Exit From \'Titans\' Alan Ritchson and Minka Kelly in Titans Image via Max In Titans , Hawk does not serve as the team\'s soaring moral guide . He was wrathful, self-destructive, and addicted to the thrill of being a vigilante. He shared a volatile relationship with Dove , full of love and pain, which added emotional weight to the series. While Titans spent much of its first three seasons developing the Bat Family’s storyline, Ritchson and Kelly grounded it in humanity. Their chemistry — alternately fiery and heartbreaking — made Hawk and Dove one of the show’s strongest pairings. By the time Season 3 rolled around, the show had found its footing. Gotham loomed large, Jason Todd ( Curran Walters ) had transformed into Red Hood , and the Titans were splintered by guilt and grief. Hawk’s death early in the season was one of the most shocking moments of the series — an emotional gut punch that reminded fans how fragile even the toughest heroes could be. In “Souls,” Ritchson’s final episode, Hank reunited with his brother Don in the afterlife, closing his arc with surprising grace. Posts By Eddie Possehl Feb 16, 2025 Ritchson later revealed that his exit wasn’t his choice. The actor told Entertainment Weekly he was “ready to move on,” but was surprised when the call came. The decision, tied to streamlining the show’s expanding cast, ultimately freed him for Reacher — and arguably, for the career leap he was always meant to make. Alan Ritchson’s Hawk Foreshadowed Potential as Batman Hawk (Alan Ritchson) in a fighting arena in \'Titans\' Image via Warner Bros. Watching Ritchson’s Titans performance today, it’s clear how perfectly it foreshadowed his later success. Hawk shared Reacher’s moral code, intimidating presence , and world-weary charm — but also his fragility. Beneath the armor and bravado, Ritchson brought vulnerability to a character who was always one punch away from breaking. It’s that combination — brute force and introspection — that’s now fueling fan campaigns to see him take on an even bigger cape: Batman. As James Gunn ’s DC Universe reboots its core heroes, Ritchson’s name has become a popular suggestion online. And it makes sense. Titans proved he can navigate the physical intensity and emotional isolation that define Bruce Wayne, while Reacher showcased the stoicism and intellect fans expect from The Dark Knight . Why \'Titans\' is Worth Your Time Wonder Girl (Conor Leslie), Aqualad (Drew Van Acker), Robin (Dick Grayson), Hawk (Alan Ritchson), Dove (Minka Kelly) in Titans Image via HBO Max Even with its plain pacing and paths that shift/stagger despite it, Titans is still one of the more interesting and ambitious shows/DC properties on television. Its shift from the DC Universe to HBO Max invested the show with a sense of higher expectations, production gloss, writing that was more engaged, and an overall more confident sense of identity — undoubtedly true in season 3. Titans offered a mix of explosive action and comfort on the characters\' journeys, from Dick Grayson\'s identity complications to Starfire\'s family drama with layers of complexity to Raven\'s almost ethereal (spiritual) journey. And through it all, Ritchson was a standout. His turn as Hawk gave the show its bruised heart, and his departure left a void that was never quite filled. For anyone who discovered him through Reacher and wants to see where that magnetism began — or for those hoping to see him don the cowl in the DCU — Titans is essential viewing. It’s a reminder that long before he towered over his enemies on Prime Video, Ritchson was already doing the heavy lifting. It\'s relaxing to spend an hour or more watching a predictable romance unfold or witnessing a character go on a transformative journey before it is time to unwrap gifts. Netflix \'s latest offering, Champagne Problems , meets the aforementioned criteria, plus the add-on benefit of stunning scenery. In it, Minka Kelly plays an ambitious executive who heads to Paris in the hopes of securing a lucrative deal with a long-standing champagne brand. As is common for most holiday titles, the protagonist goes on a business trip only to find a handsome and conveniently available French man to show her the city. With a European backdrop, romance between the leads, and champagne to spare (filling up a champagne glass while watching this would be fitting), this Netflix rom-com is poised to not only bring the jolly spirit back to full force but satisfy a craving for travel for those unable to plan a getaway abroad. What Is \'Champagne Problems\' About? When Sydney Price (Kelly) is faced with a major career opportunity, she takes it without hesitation. Yet, while she prepares to take off to Paris with a clear goal in mind, she makes a promise to her sister that she will at least take one night off from her trip to do some sightseeing and ultimately rediscover who she is and what she wants beyond her job. Despite being driven by the prospect of acquiring Château Cassell, a beloved French champagne house, she does free up her itinerary to pay a visit to a local bookstore, where she meets Henri Cassell ( Tom Wozniczka ). As expected, sparks fly instantly, with Sydney being drawn to him the more they spend time together, having some macaroons and hot chocolate while admiring the Eiffel Tower at night. Related ‘Ransom Canyon’ and ‘Slow Horses’ Stars Soak in the Magic of Paris at Christmas in New ‘Champagne Problems’ Image [Exclusive] Thibault de Montalemert also stars in the romantic holiday comedy coming to Netflix this month. Posts By Ryan O\'Rourke Nov 10, 2025 Although their eventful evening seems like a dream reality, Sydney is reminded the next day that the whole reason she is there is to make sure that she lands the deal and returns to her company with good news. Yet, to the protagonist\'s surprise, Henri is the son of Hugo Cassell ( Thibault de Montalembert ), the very person she came to Paris to negotiate with. As Sydney spends the weekend with Hugo, Henri, and other bidders, she is not only one step closer to making the acquisition happen, but becoming even more emotionally attached to the people she is with and the places she visits . \'Champagne Problems\' Feels Like a Scenic Getaway Tom Wozniczka and Minka Kelly in Champagne Problems Image via Netflix Champagne Problems might fit the bill for rom-com lovers seeking their next holiday watch , but it will also appeal to those who are on the lookout for their next holiday escape . Filmed in Paris, as well as Épernay and Reims, the film feels like a stunning venture into the places that Sydney visits throughout it, making viewers feel like they are just as much part of the experience. The main character has been so focused on making it professionally, that she has never gotten to travel for fun. As much as she travels to France for work, she gets to finally do something for her own enjoyment, and open herself to the prospect of love. Although the film does focus on her and Henri, Champagne Problems also features a mismatched group of buyers competing with Sydney to acquire Château Cassell. Amongst them are party animal Roberto Salazar ( Sean Amsing ), German misfit Otto Moller ( Flula Borg ), and the hostile-yet-driven Brigitte Laurent ( Astrid Whettnall ). Each of their different personalities dictate the ways in which they try to convince Hugo to sell his champagne empire, and it\'s entertaining to see their persuasion tactics put into motion. Although the supporting characters are primarily one-dimensional and stereotypical, their presence doesn\'t hinder the fun viewers have while watching them bond and go head-to-head in this civilized bidding war . Minka Kelly Is a Winning Christmas Rom-Com Lead in \'Champagne Problems\' Yet, without a doubt, Champagne Problems \' greatest asset is Minka Kelly. The Friday Night Lights alum, who recently graced the screen on Netflix\'s Ransom Canyon , proves to be a romantic lead worth rooting for . She isn\'t the typical iteration of the businesswoman we see in rom-coms like this. She might be passionate about her job, but she isn\'t the type of person looking to pick a fight in order to get what she wants. Throughout the film, Sydney lets go of her planner-oriented mindset and gives into the experience, not only becoming friends with Roberto, but also finding the love of her life. Kelly and Wozniczka, who many might know from Slow Horses , have just the right amount of chemistry to keep you invested. Their stroll through the Christmas market earlier in the film and their sweet exchange at the bookstore towards the end are the highlights of their romantic storyline. Although the couple do not share as much time on screen together as one would hope, writer-director Mark Steven Johnson made the right call in focusing on Sydney\'s path to self-discovery. As Hallmark-esque as this Netflix rom-com might be , it offers the perfect combo for what you anticipate from a seasonal title . It delivers on a low-stakes love story between two people from different cultural backgrounds, allows for its main character to grow into her own and understand her worth, and gives viewers the opportunity to escape to Paris without leaving their couch. Its supporting cast might not get the opportunity to go beyond their stereotypical constructs and the main pair might not get as many swoon-worthy sequences together as many might\'ve desired, but the film is able to check off all the boxes you would hope for. But more importantly, it makes a case for Kelly to join Kat Graham and Lindsay Lohan as part of the roster of romantic leads in Netflix holiday rom-coms. If this was her first foray into the Christmas movie pipeline, the hope is that it is certainly not her last. Champagne Problems is now available to stream on Netflix. Titans , which premiered on DC Universe in 2018 (and is now available on HBO Max), adapted the Teen Titans mythology and added an edge. The series followed Dick Grayson ( Brenton Thwaites ) as he emerged from Batman\'s death and created the next generation of heroes, including Starfire ( Anna Diop ), Raven ( Teagan Croft ), and Beast Boy ( Ryan Potter ). Ritchson was introduced into the series as Hank Hall, better known as Hawk — a battered, brutish hand-to-hand fighting vigilante who, along with Dove ( Minka Kelly ), brought street-level brutality and raw emotion to a series frequently teetering between superhero visuals and down-to-earth drama. For viewers who know Ritchson as the taciturn, near-superhuman Jack Reacher, Titans is the final piece of the puzzle that shows how long he has been capable of being the leading man of a franchise. What To Know About Alan Ritchson\'s Exit From \'Titans\' Alan Ritchson and Minka Kelly in Titans Image via Max In Titans , Hawk does not serve as the team\'s soaring moral guide . He was wrathful, self-destructive, and addicted to the thrill of being a vigilante. He shared a volatile relationship with Dove , full of love and pain, which added emotional weight to the series. While Titans spent much of its first three seasons developing the Bat Family’s storyline, Ritchson and Kelly grounded it in humanity. Their chemistry — alternately fiery and heartbreaking — made Hawk and Dove one of the show’s strongest pairings. By the time Season 3 rolled around, the show had found its footing. Gotham loomed large, Jason Todd ( Curran Walters ) had transformed into Red Hood , and the Titans were splintered by guilt and grief. Hawk’s death early in the season was one of the most shocking moments of the series — an emotional gut punch that reminded fans how fragile even the toughest heroes could be. In “Souls,” Ritchson’s final episode, Hank reunited with his brother Don in the afterlife, closing his arc with surprising grace. Posts By Eddie Possehl Feb 16, 2025 Ritchson later revealed that his exit wasn’t his choice. The actor told Entertainment Weekly he was “ready to move on,” but was surprised when the call came. The decision, tied to streamlining the show’s expanding cast, ultimately freed him for Reacher — and arguably, for the career leap he was always meant to make. Alan Ritchson’s Hawk Foreshadowed Potential as Batman Hawk (Alan Ritchson) in a fighting arena in \'Titans\' Image via Warner Bros. Watching Ritchson’s Titans performance today, it’s clear how perfectly it foreshadowed his later success. Hawk shared Reacher’s moral code, intimidating presence , and world-weary charm — but also his fragility. Beneath the armor and bravado, Ritchson brought vulnerability to a character who was always one punch away from breaking. It’s that combination — brute force and introspection — that’s now fueling fan campaigns to see him take on an even bigger cape: Batman. As James Gunn ’s DC Universe reboots its core heroes, Ritchson’s name has become a popular suggestion online. And it makes sense. Titans proved he can navigate the physical intensity and emotional isolation that define Bruce Wayne, while Reacher showcased the stoicism and intellect fans expect from The Dark Knight . Why \'Titans\' is Worth Your Time Wonder Girl (Conor Leslie), Aqualad (Drew Van Acker), Robin (Dick Grayson), Hawk (Alan Ritchson), Dove (Minka Kelly) in Titans Image via HBO Max Even with its plain pacing and paths that shift/stagger despite it, Titans is still one of the more interesting and ambitious shows/DC properties on television. Its shift from the DC Universe to HBO Max invested the show with a sense of higher expectations, production gloss, writing that was more engaged, and an overall more confident sense of identity — undoubtedly true in season 3. Titans offered a mix of explosive action and comfort on the characters\' journeys, from Dick Grayson\'s identity complications to Starfire\'s family drama with layers of complexity to Raven\'s almost ethereal (spiritual) journey. And through it all, Ritchson was a standout. His turn as Hawk gave the show its bruised heart, and his departure left a void that was never quite filled. For anyone who discovered him through Reacher and wants to see where that magnetism began — or for those hoping to see him don the cowl in the DCU — Titans is essential viewing. It’s a reminder that long before he towered over his enemies on Prime Video, Ritchson was already doing the heavy lifting. Production on the Searchlight film begins this fall. David Harbour and Eva Victor are also attached to star. Sanne Wohlenberg, one of Gilroy’s top lieutenants on “Andor,” will produce alongside him, with fellow “Andor” vet Damián García serving as cinematographer. When TheWrap last spoke to Gilroy , he said that the experience of making “Andor” is directly influencing his approach on “Behemoth!” “I just think that the system that we made, the workflow and how we don’t let anything fester for more than a moment, how we deal with everything as it comes in, and how everybody knows everything [will be utilized],” he said. “I think our highly communicative community, spiritual teamwork approach to making things — I think it took a long time to evolve, for us to perfect that. I think the model that we made is a model I would like to use in all creative projects going forward. Movies Olivia Wilde Joins Andor Creator’s Star-Studded Movie October 28, 2025 By Maggie Dela Paz Don’t Worry Darling actress-director Olivia Wilde has signed on to join the cast of Searchlight Pictures ‘ music drama, titled Behemoth! , which hails from Andor creator Tony Gilroy . Wilde is expected to play the main character’s former lover. Besides Behemoth!, Wilde will also next be seen in the erotic thriller movie I Want Your Sex, and in the comedy movie The Invite, which she will also be directing. She most recently appeared in the first season of Apple TV’s newest comedy show, The Studio, where she played a version of herself. What do we know about Andor creator’s Behemoth! movie? According to THR, the story is “a love letter to the music of the movies and the people who make it. It tells of a musician from a family of musicians who returns to Los Angeles.” Behemoth! will be directed by Gilroy, who also wrote the movie’s screenplay. Wilde will be joining previously announced cast members Pedro Pascal (The Fantastic Four: First Steps) and David Harbour (Thunderbolts*), who will also both appear in Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday. In addition, rising filmmaker Eva Victor (Sorry, Baby) has also joined the cast. Production is expected to begin later this week in Los Angeles. The star-studded movie is also being produced by Tony Gilroy, Sanne Wohlenberg, and John Gilroy, who all previously worked together on the acclaimed Star Wars series Andor. Searchlight Pictures executives Rayne Roberts and Cameron Chidsey are overseeing the project on behalf of the studio. Earlier this year, she appeared in Rogen\'s Apple TV+ series The Studio. She last appeared on the big screen in Damien Chazelle\'s Babylon and the thriller Don\'t Worry Darling, which she also directed, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Her diverse body of acting work includes Her, Babylon, Cowboys & Aliens, Tron: Legacy, A Vigilante, 1984 on Broadway, and the Emmy-winning series "House". Cunniff and Bronte Payne have been named the co-heads of film at LuckyChap . Cunniff joins the Barbie banner as an executive VP of film from Black Bear, with Payne, a LuckyChap veteran, being upped to executive VP of film. At Black Bear, Cunniff executive-produced upcoming titles like Greg Araki’s I Want Your Sex , starring Olivia Wilde, and Tuner , the Telluride and TIFF title from Oscar winner Daniel Roher. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 16 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The arrival of Tron: Ares in 2025 was supposed to reignite one of Disney’s most visually iconic franchises. Instead, it landed with an underwhelming thud. Few viewers have championed it as a meaningful evolution of the Grid, and the film’s divisive reception made its long-delayed release feel even more anticlimactic. I found myself thinking more about the franchise’s missed opportunities than its future. Tron has never become the flagship multimedia powerhouse Disney hoped for, but the franchise isn’t without high points. The original 1982 Tron is still beloved for its groundbreaking digital aesthetic, and Tron: Legacy, while not as widely adored, remains an ambitious, visually intoxicating sequel. Compared to Ares, Legacy at least felt like a continuation that understood the world it inherited. However, the best addition to the Tron universe is also its most overlooked. The single-season DisneyXD animated series Tron: Uprising remains one of the strongest narrative expansions the franchise has ever produced. If Disney genuinely wants to build a more cohesive future for the Grid, revisiting Uprising should be a priority. Tron: Uprising Was A Prequel To Tron: Legacy Uprising Showed The Grid At Its Narrative Peak Three characters stare out at a virtual landscape in Tron Uprising Tron: Uprising premiered in 2012 as a sleek, visually striking prequel bridging the gap between Tron and Tron: Legacy . The series followed Beck (voiced by Elijah Wood), a young program who rises against Clu’s oppressive regime under the mentorship of Tron (voiced by Bruce Boxleitner). It delivered a richer exploration of life inside the Grid than either of the films managed. What made Uprising so compelling was its commitment to character growth and rebellion, elements the films only brushed past. Beck’s evolution from hesitant mechanic to masked revolutionary gave the series an emotional core, while Tron’s wounded, battle-scarred presence added a grounded mentor dynamic rarely seen on DisneyXD. Even supporting characters like General Tesler (Lance Henriksen) and Paige (Emmanuelle Chriqui) were layered with surprising nuance. The animation style - angular, neon-drenched, and heavily inspired by Legacy’s design sensibilities - pushed television visuals forward. Combined with a pulsing score inspired by Daft Punk’s Tron: Legacy soundtrack , the show captured the cyberpunk tone of the franchise far better than the admittedly aesthetically sleek Ares managed. Despite lasting only one season, Tron: Uprising proved the Grid could sustain long-form storytelling. Its world-building, atmosphere, and serialized structure remain unmatched within the franchise, making it the most polished expansion Tron has ever received. Disney Moved Away From Tron: Legacy Too Fast Legacy Modernized Tron In A Way The Franchise Should Have Expanded Jeff Bridges in awe as Kevin Flynn in Tron Legacy While not universally adored, 2010’s Tron: Legacy was a confident modernization of the original film’s ideas. It followed Sam Flynn (Garrett Hedlund) and Quorra (Olivia Wilde) as they navigated a darker, more mature Grid. The movie’s neon-drenched visuals, philosophical underpinnings, and Daft Punk’s instantly iconic score made it a bold sequel that respected its roots. Tron: Legacy wasn’t perfect , but it provided fertile ground for expansion. It introduced a world of exiled programs, evolving isomorphic lifeforms, and a Grid on the brink of collapse - threads ripe for follow-up storytelling. Uprising embraced these elements, but Disney’s Tron movie strategy abandoned them too quickly. Tron: Ares made only superficial references to Legacy , opting for a thematic detour rather than a continuation. The absence of Sam and Quorra as central figures created a jarring disconnect. Instead of building on Legacy ’s momentum, Ares felt like a soft reboot hoping to stand alone without the narrative framework fans valued. Disney’s pivot away from Legacy weakened the franchise’s cohesion . A more direct sequel could have capitalized on the film’s lingering plotlines, expanded its mythology, and maintained continuity that viewers were ready to invest in. Tron: Ares Should Have Been A Proper Sequel To Legacy Ares Ignored The Franchise’s Strongest Story Threads Ares locking into his lightcycle in Tron Ares The biggest issue with Tron: Ares wasn’t its ambition, it was the disconnect from the franchise that spawned it. The movie introduced Ares (Jared Leto) as a program crossing into the human world, an idea intriguing in theory but executed far from the established tone of the franchise. The narrative felt isolated, drifting away from the emotional and thematic foundation laid by Legacy . The tonal shift was particularly noticeable. Legacy balanced sleek futurism with melancholy introspection. Ares opted for a conventional sci-fi aesthetic that rarely resembled the Grid audiences knew. Without continuing Sam and Quorra’s story, the Tron: Ares narrative felt cut adrift from the characters who shaped the modern era of Tron . Had Ares picked up immediately after Legacy , the franchise could have explored Quorra’s transition into the human world, the fate of the Grid, and the repercussions of Clu’s defeat. These threads were rich enough to support multiple films, yet were left untouched. Ultimately, Ares proved that Tron works best when it leans into continuity. A proper sequel to Legacy would have strengthened the franchise instead of fragmenting it further, and revisiting Tron: Uprising shows exactly how strong that direction could have been. The auteur was honored at the Museum of Modern Art’s annual Film Benefit, in recognition of her era-defining contributions to cinema. The evening, presented by Chanel, made for a suitably starry reunion. The Oscar-winning filmmaker’s muses and collaborators were out in force. Elle Fanning, who was directed by Coppola in the 2010 flick Somewhere , turned up in a cream-hued embellished Spring 2026 dress to celebrate her. Also thrilled to be wearing a runway-fresh creation by Matthieu Blazy, Lupita Nyong’o. “It’s a milestone moment, I would say,” she said, happy to support Coppola on her big night. “I really loved her film Priscilla . It is quite an achievement for someone to the tell the story of a woman who really had no agency, but with agency, so I was really moved by her story telling.” Marc Jacobs, the subject of Coppola’s new documentary Marc by Sofia , was proud as punch, as was designer Anna Sui. The latter is not only a longtime friend, she also created pieces for the aforementioned Priscilla biopic. When Coppola’s social media-famous daughters Romy and Cosima Croquette spotted Jacobs and Sui, they immediately embraced them. As Coppola herself took to the red carpet, the stylish doppelgänger duo—and their dad, Thomas Mars—eagerly snapped videos of her. Aughts heartthrob Josh Hartnett, who would later take to the stage to give remarks about working with Coppola, told Vogue: “Sofia taught me how to be bold. I don’t know if you know this, but she wrote the script for The Virgin Suicides after the producers told her not to. She was not known in Hollywood at the time and she hadn’t directed anything or written anything that had been produced, so it was a shot in the dark. She was basically just someone who loved the book and felt compelled to write it for the screen. And once the producers read it, they thought it was beautiful and hired her to direct.” Further illustrating how involved she is as a director, he laughed at a memory that she even helped him cut his wig for the seminal 1999 film. After guests, including Rose Byrne and Olivia Wilde, caught up over cocktails, they ascended the museum’s candlelit staircases for the gala’s seated dinner and program. Elle Fanning—who first worked with Coppola when she was 11-years-old—regaled the room with tales about how the director defined girlhood for her. “I like to say, while I didn’t go to college, I went to New Orleans with Sofia, Kirsten Dunst, and Nicole Kidman [for The Beguiled ], and it was there that Sofia shaped me at a another formative period of my life when I was 18.” The night continued with speeches from Bill Murray, Coppola’s brother Roman Coppola, and her cousin, Jason Schwartzman, as well as a pre-recorded video from her longtime muse Kirsten Dunst. David Letterman also announced a surprise musical performance by Elvis Costello—an artist whom Sofia and Roman listened to religiously while growing up—while pink trays of sweet petite fours did the rounds. A cinematic tribute, indeed.
