WATCH NOW \'Weeds\' (2005–2012) Credit: Alamy Starring: Mary-Louise Parker, Mary-Kate Olsen, Elizabeth Perkins, Justin Kirk, Tonye Patano, and Romany Malco Why it makes the list: There was no shortage of dark dramedies on premium cable in the 2000s, but only one was powerful enough to lure Mary-Kate Olsen to the small screen. This Showtime offering followed a suburban single mother (Parker) through her decision to start selling marijuana to support her family’s upper-middle-class lifestyle after the untimely death of her husband. WATCH NOW \'The West Wing\' (1999–2006) Credit: NBC Starring: Martin Sheen, Rob Lowe, Allison Janney, John Spencer, and Bradley Whitford Why it makes the list: A fair share of political dramas center around the White House, and we owe them all to this bad boy right here. Countless scandals, threats, and political scuffles ran amok over the series\' seven seasons, and the show introduced us to a ton of stars we still love today. WATCH NOW \'The Wire\' (2002–2008) Credit: HBO Starring: Dominic West, Wendell Pierce, Lance Reddick, Sonja Sohn, John Doman, and Deirdre Lovejoy Why it makes the list: Every part of the drug food chain, from addicts and dealers to cops and politicians, gets dissected in this gritty HBO drama set in Baltimore. Narcos , who? WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Mystery TV Shows \'Alias\' (2001–2006) Credit: Alamy Starring: Jennifer Garner , Ron Rifkin, Carl Lumbly, Kevin Weisman, and Victor Garber Why it makes the list: Watching a fresh-faced Garner kick some ass for a secret branch of the CIA is just what the doctor ordered! Also, a young Bradley Cooper appears in several episodes, so our complaints are minimal. WATCH NOW \'The Closer\' (2005–2012) Credit: Alamy/AJ Pics Starring: Kyra Sedgwick, J. K. Simmons, Corey Reynolds, Robert Gossett, G.W. Bailey, and Tony Denison Why it makes the list: Everyone loves a gripping crime show , and The Closer gives the genre a good dose of girl power. LAPD Deputy Chief Brenda Leigh Johnson (Sedgwick) is smart, tough, and hellbent on getting her man—even if it means breaking a rule of her own to get the job done. Basically? She’s a total boss. WATCH NOW \'Dexter\' (2006–2013) Credit: Alamy Starring: Michael C. Hall, Julie Benz, Jennifer Carpenter, Erik King, and Lauren Vélez Why it makes the list: Dexter put a fresh spin on the classic whodunnit by making its titular forensic analyst a vigilante serial killer by night. The series remained so popular that it spawned a follow-up limited series in 2021 and a prequel series that debuted in late 2024. WATCH NOW \'Ghost Whisperer\' 2005–2012) Credit: CBS Starring: Jennifer Love Hewitt , David Conrad, Camryn Manheim, Jamie Kennedy, Aisha Tyler, and Jay Mohr Why it makes the list: Between her movies, music videos (we’ll never get LFO’s “Girl on TV” out of our heads!), and her iconic Neutrogena commercials, Jennifer Love Hewitt was seemingly never in one spot for too long in the late ‘90s. By the time the mid-2000s rolled around, however, fans could count on seeing her every week as Melinda Gordon on Ghost Whisperer . Her character pulled double-duty as an antique shop owner and paranormal communicator with a side hustle involving helping countless trapped souls set their spirits at ease over the course of the show’s seven-year run. WATCH NOW \'Monk\' (2002–2009) Credit: Alamy Starring: Tony Shalhoub, Bitty Schram, Jason Gray-Stanford, Ted Levine, and Traylor Howard Why it makes the list: Another still-beloved gem, Monk centers on Adrian Monk (Tony Shaloub), a titular detective who must grapple with obsessive-compulsive disorder, germophobia, and a host of other mental health issues while simultaneously solving various mysteries and solving his wife’s cold case murder. Fun fact: Monk ’s 2009 finale once held the record for the most-watched scripted cable drama. (It was later overtaken by zombies with an episode of The Walking Dead. ) WATCH NOW \'Veronica Mars\' (2004–2007; 2019) Credit: Alamy Starring: Kristen Bell , Percy Daggs III, Teddy Dunn, Jason Dohring, and Enrico Colantoni Why it makes the list: Bell plays the titular detective in this mid-aughts show, which blended teen drama and crime into one extra-sharp and smartly written series. Fans loved it so much that they crowdfunded a movie version in 2014, which in turn inspired Hulu to take up the mantle and put out a belated fourth season of the show in 2019. WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Reality TV Shows \'America’s Next Top Model\' (2003-2018) Credit: The CW Starring: Tyra Banks , Janice Dickinson, Nigel Barker, Twiggy, Jay Manuel, J. Alexander Why it makes the list: If you aren’t wondering whatever happened to ANTM winners Adrianne Curry, Eva Marcille, or CariDee English every once in a blue moon, you probably didn’t come up in the 2000s. With its weekly photoshoots, go-see challenges, and mind-blowing/traumatic makeovers, each cycle of ANTM proved more memorable than the last. (Though nothing will ever top the moment Tyra lost her cool on a contestant and instantly became a time-honored meme .) WATCH NOW \'The City\' (2008–2010) Credit: Alamy/Wenn Rights Ltd. Starring: Whitney Port, Olivia Palermo, Erin Kaplan, Joe Zee, Kelly Cutrone, and Roxy Olin Why it makes the list: The City had all the drama we loved from The Hills and upped the fashion stakes. It follows Lauren’s former Teen Vogue co-intern, Whitney Port, as she embarks on a journey to become a respected fashion designer. If only she could get her frenemy Olivia Palermo from the Elle accessories department on board… WATCH NOW \'The Girls Next Door\' (2005–2010) Credit: Alamy Starring: Holly Madison, Bridget Marquardt, Kendra Wilkinson, and Hugh Hefner Why it makes the list: Love it or hate it, the Playboy Mansion and its female inhabitants became a cultural phenomenon in the mid-\'00s with the debut of the reality series The Girls Next Door . Rather than focusing on the mansion’s infamous owner, Hugh Hefner, the series shone a spotlight on the women who lived inside its walls: namely, Holly Madison, Bridget Marquardt, and Kendra Wilkinson. Madison later called it “ the most bizarre show that was ever on television ,” citing the family-friendly packaging of their taboo and highly sexualized reality, which she later detailed in a 2015 tell-all book . WATCH NOW \'The Hills\' (2006–2010) Credit: MTV Starring: Lauren Conrad, Kristin Cavallari, Audrina Patridge, Brody Jenner, Heidi Montag, Spencer Pratt, and Justin Bobby Why it makes the list: Released in 2006, The Hills was a natural progression for fans of Laguna Beach , who followed heroine Lauren Conrad’s move from her idyllic hometown to the big bad city. She got a whole lot more than a new zip code, including an internship at Teen Vogue , a new crush or two (ahem, Brody Jenner), and plenty of new fun-loving besties to help her navigate life in the Hollywood Hills. WATCH NOW \'Laguna Beach\' (2004–2006) Credit: Getty Images Starring: Lauren Conrad, Kristin Cavallari , Stephen Colletti, Lo Bosworth, and Talan Torriero Why it makes the list: Laguna Beach walked so that The Hills could run! We\'re forever thankful to MTV for following eight Laguna Beach teens during their last years of high school, creating high-quality entertainment (and a whole new vernacular—donezo, anyone?) in the process. WATCH NOW \'Punk\'d\' (2003–2015) Credit: MTV Starring: Ashton Kutcher Why it makes the list: Watching your favorite celebs get secretly pranked by other A-listers (its host was Ashton Kutcher) was peak reality television. How many of them kept cool during the high-stress situations is astounding. WATCH NOW \'Rock of Love with Bret Michaels\' (2007–2009) Credit: VH1 Starring: Brett Michaels Why it makes the list: Long before there was Love Island , there was Rock of Love —the raunchy, over-the-top dating show that gave glam metal groupies the chance to date Bret Michaels, a.k.a. the lead singer of Poison. If you’ve never seen this one, let’s say you’re in for a treat: These ladies make The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives crew look tame. WATCH NOW \'The Simple Life\' (2003–2007) Credit: Alamy Starring: Paris Hilton and Nicole Richie Why it makes the list: This "reality" series about two Hollywood socialites ditching their designer handbags and extravagant ways to live like "the middle class" is \'00s reality TV at its best. Our favorite line? "What is Walmart?" WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Teen Shows \'Dawson\'s Creek\' (1998–2003) Credit: Alamy Starring: James Van Der Beek, Katie Holmes , Michelle Williams, Joshua Jackson, and Busy Philipps Why it makes the list: The 2000s were the golden age of teen drama, and none led the charge quite like Dawson’s Creek . It follows the intertwined everyday dramas of Dawson Leery (Van Der Beek) and his closest friends throughout their high school (and early college) days in a small New England town while tackling a range of real-world issues such as classism, homophobia, and mental health. WATCH NOW \'Degrassi: The Next Generation\' (2001–2015) Credit: CTV Starring : Miriam McDonald, Shane Kippel, Cassie Steele, Lauren Collins, Stefan Brogren, and Drake Why it makes the list : Degrassi was the Canadian drama of the \'00s with its honest depictions of real-life problems affecting teens (bullying, teen pregnancy, school shootings) and its knockout cast that featured several generations of young stars. WATCH NOW \'Freaks and Geeks\' (1999–2000) Credit: Alamy Starring: Linda Cardellini, John Francis Daley, James Franco, Busy Philipps, Seth Rogen, and Jason Segel Why it makes the list: Unlike other canceled-too-soon shows on this list that were later revived or turned into feature films down the line, Freaks and Geeks remains a one-season wonder. But that hasn’t stopped the Judd Apatow-produced series from becoming a beloved cult classic, thanks to its spot-on depiction of high school’s often impossible-to-navigate social system. WATCH NOW \'Friday Night Lights\' (2006–2011) Credit: Alamy Starring: Kyle Chandler, Taylor Kitsch, Brad Leland, Connie Britton, Aimee Teegarden, and Zach Gilford Why it makes the list: Say it with us, "Clear eyes. Full hearts. Can\'t lose." While we can\'t technically attend a Dillon Panthers football game (ugh), Friday Night Lights was one of the strongest and most well-executed teen dramas of its time, tackling topics like racism and teen pregnancy through a whole new lens. WATCH NOW \'Gilmore Girls\' (2000–2007) Credit: Alamy Starring: Lauren Graham, Alexis Bledel, Milo Ventimiglia, Jared Padalecki, Scott Patterson, and Melissa McCarthy Why it makes the list: Forget Team Conrad or Team Jere: Back in the 2000s, it was Team Dean, Team Jess, or Team Logan. And we have Rory Gilmore and her crippling inability to make a proper decision on Gilmore Girls to thank for it. WATCH NOW \'Glee\' (2009–2015) Credit: Fox Starring: Chris Colfer, Jane Lynch, Lea Michele, Kevin McHale, Matthew Morrison, Naya Rivera, Corey Monteith, and Amber Riley Why it makes the list: Every theatre kid’s dream come true, Glee set high school antics to the soundtrack of the ‘00s, making it a time capsule of sorts for those who didn’t get to revel in all of the era’s adolescent glory firsthand. The guest appearances didn’t suck, either: everyone from Britney Spears and Gwyneth Paltrow to John Stamos and Sarah Jessica Parker made a cameo. WATCH NOW \'Gossip Girl\' (2008–2012) Credit: The CW Starring: Blake Lively , Leighton Meester , Penn Badgley, Taylor Momsen, Ed Westwick, and Chace Crawford Why it makes the list: What\'s better than watching a bunch of hot, wealthy New York socialites get in all sorts of messy drama while simultaneously trying to avoid becoming the wrath of Gossip Girl , a.k.a. the most life-ruining anonymous gossip blog, like, ever? Nothing, of course. This one also gets major bonus points for the weekly style inspo . WATCH NOW \'The O.C.\' (2003–2007) Credit: Fox Starring: Ben McKenzie, Mischa Barton , Adam Brody , Rachel Bilson , Peter Gallagher, and Kelly Rowan Why it makes the list: Fun fact: This teenage soap drama set in Southern California\'s Newport Beach was the inspiration for MTV\'s Laguna Beach . It also features a baby-faced Adam Brody trying to survive high school before he was making us all swoon on Nobody Wants This . WATCH NOW \'One Tree Hill\' (2003–2012) Credit: Collection Christophel Starring: Chad Michael Murray , James Lafferty, Hilarie Burton, Bethany Joy Lenz, Sophia Bush , and Lee Norris Why it makes the list: This high school drama set in Tree Hill, North Carolina can get a bit cheesy at times, but it\'s also a coming-of-age staple that paved the way for the Riverdale set, so we\'re going to go ahead and give credit where credit is due. WATCH NOW \'Popular\' (1999–2001) Credit: The WB Starring: Leslie Bibb, Carly Pope, Sara Rue, Tamara Mello, Leslie Grossman, Christopher Gorham, and Tammy Lynn Michaels Why it makes the list: There’s a reason Leslie Bibb rocked the cunty little bob so hard in White Lotus —it wasn’t her first rodeo. In the early 2000s, her Popular character Brooke McQueen had a similar cut to match her mean girl (eventually turned sweet) persona. More than just giving us her fabulous coif, however, this show was a harbinger of great teen drama to come as HBIC Brooke is forced to move in with the studious Sam McPherson (Pope) when their parents get engaged. \'Smallville (2001-2011) Credit: The WB Starring: Tom Welling, Allison Mack, Kristin Kreuk, Michael Rosenbaum, Erica Durance, Justin Hartley Why it makes the list: What if Superman grew up in small-town Kansas and had to deal with the trials and tribulations of everyday life as a teen before he learned how to harness his superpowers to save the world? Such is the plot of Smallville. It also gives some backstory to his early relationships with Lois Lane (Durance) and Lex Luthor (Rosenbaum). WATCH NOW \'Supernatural\' (2005–2020) Credit: The CW Starring: Jensen Ackles, Jared Padalecki, Misha Collins, and Jeffrey Dean Morgan Why it makes the list: Demons, witches, vampires, ghosts: This show had it all! If its ghouls and goblins didn’t haunt your dreams between 2005 and 2020, the two (very handsome) demon-hunting brothers at its center, Dean and Sam Winchester (Jensen Ackles and Jared Padalecki), were bound to. WATCH NOW \'The Vampire Diaries\' (2009–2017) Credit: The CW Starring: Paul Wesley, Ian Somerhalder, Nina Dobrev , Kat Graham, Candice King Why it makes the list: If the love triangle between Edward, Jacob, and Bella in Twilight had you in a tizzy, there was no way you were missing The Vampire Diaries. The CW hit took the stakes up a notch by creating romantic tension for high school student Elena Gilbert (Dobrev) with two vampire brothers (Wesley and Somerhalder) with a knack for falling for the same girl. The tone of this ‘00s home run is slightly darker than the YA novel-turned-film, however, so be prepared for a lot more bloodshed. Inquiries: archie.f@movieweb.com Sign in to your MovieWeb account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap One of the most iconic sci-fi series from the 2010s has been a staple of Netflix\'s streaming library. But the seven-season series is about to leave streaming, and no one yet knows where it will move to. While the 20th Century was arguably the golden age for sci-fi TV, people tend to forget how good the 2010s were. Stranger Things , Westworld , Dark , The Expanse , Black Mirror , The Mandalorian , Love, Death + Robots , and the criminally underrated Legion all debuted during that decade. But ask any CW binge-watcher which sci-fi series dominated the 2010s, and they\'ll undoubtedly answer The 100 . Unfortunately, like the human survivors abandoning The Ark, The 100 is about to leave Netflix. The show will vacate Netflix\'s streaming library on December 18. That\'s right, all seven seasons of The 100 will no longer stream on Netflix from December. The show\'s removal from Netflix comes alongside the streamer\'s culling of several popular shows from its content library. As well as The 100 , Supernatural and Arrow (another CW hit) will also leave Netflix in December. The 100 is based on the young adult sci-fi series of the same name written by Kass Morgan. The four books in the series were turned into a seven-season show on The CW, which debuted in 2014 and ran until 2020. The story itself takes place almost a century after nuclear war has destroyed the Earth. The few surviving humans fled to outer space on a giant self-sufficient station known as The Ark. But when The Ark begins to shut down, 100 juveniles are sent down to Earth to see if it is safe to return. The official synopsis reads: "When nuclear Armageddon destroys civilization on Earth, the only survivors are those on the 12 international space stations in orbit at the time. Three generations later, the 4,000 survivors living on a space ark of linked stations see their resources dwindle and face Draconian measures established to ensure humanity\'s future. Desperately looking for a solution, the ark\'s leaders send 100 juvenile prisoners back to the planet to test its habitability. Having always lived in space, the exiles find the planet fascinating and terrifying, but with the fate of the human race in their hands, they must forge a path into the unknown." \'The 100\' Divided Critics & Audiences During Its Run Eliza Taylor in the 100. The CW Like many of The CW\'s best shows, The 100 got off to a tremendous start. Season 1 received decent reviews from both critics and audiences, holding a 76% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a stronger audience score of 78%. Season 2 was ever more well received, earning a prestigious 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a strong audience score of 87%. "Best show on TV. I liked The Black List and Arrow before, but this one is far better. Still like the others, but this one is well written and keeps you guessing," wrote one user after watching the second season. The 100 experienced a strange phenomenon in its later seasons. Seasons 5, 6, and 7 are all 100% rated on Rotten Tomatoes from critics\' reviews. However, audiences slowly fell off with the final seasons. Season 7, which was released in May 2020, holds a measly audience score of just 42%, compared to its perfect critics\' rating. Studios Movies Movie News Movie Reviews Thunderbolts* Jurassic World Rebirth Superman Fantastic Four: First Steps Avatar: Fire and Ash Avengers: Doomsday TV TV News TV Reviews The Last of Us Andor Peacemaker Ironheart Alien: Earth Squid Game Gaming Gaming News Video Game Reviews Nintendo Xbox PlayStation PC Anime Anime News Dragon Ball Demon Slayer Jujutsu Kaisen Naruto My Hero Academia One Piece Franchises DC Marvel Star Wars The Walking Dead Star Trek Power Rangers Shop Forum Facebook X YouTube Instagram Google Discover Google Top Posts TV Shows 5 Sci-Fi Shows That Wished They Were Lost By Niall Gray November 9, 2025, 11:30am Comments Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Ever since it first appeared on screens in 2004, Lost has been emulated by countless other shows. Following the survivors of a plane crash as they uncover various mysteries on a desert island, Lost captivated audiences around the world almost instantly. Sadly, Lost became an example of a great TV show that was terrible by the end , but despite its disappointing finale, the ABC show outlived even its own massive success. It is often credited with revolutionizing the format of modern television, focusing on wider story arcs rather than dedicating itself to an episodic format. In that sense, Lost is one of the most influential shows in modern history. Videos by ComicBook.com Understanding how popular Lost was during its run is key to understanding why so many shows in the years since have tried to recreate its magic. Since it ended, many TV shows have tried to be the new Lost and failed, while others have found success but not managed to recreate Lost ‘s unique brand of tense drama. While several sci-fi shows have attempted to emulate Lost , some were able to do so to much better effect than others. Read Next 7 Most Infuriating Lost Storylines and Plots 5) Travelers (Netflix, 2016-2018) One of the very few truly great time travel TV shows , Netflix’s Travelers is criminally underrated. Its high-concept story concerns survivors in a post-apocalyptic future who are able to project their consciousnesses back through time, living through hosts with the intention of preventing the apocalypse. After running for three seasons across 34 episodes, Travelers was prematurely canceled. Travelers could easily have become the new Lost , had it found a way to reach a wider audience. For all its narrative potential and mysterious plot developments, Travelers simply didn’t land high enough viewership to reach the levels of popularity enjoyed by Lost . As great as the show could have been, its ratings also led to its cancellation, dooming it to never quite reach its full potential. 4) Under the Dome (CBS, 2013-2015) Although there are many great Stephen King movies , there aren’t as many noteworthy TV shows based on the iconic author’s works. One of the lesser-known attempts to bring a King story to life on the small screen is Under the Dome , which aired on CBS between 2013 and 2015 before coming to an end. Despite initial ratings seeming promising, viewership fell off sharply in the show’s second and third seasons. The decline in ratings is a big reason why Under the Dome couldn’t be the new Lost . Although it contended with similar themes, including a central mystery and a heavy emphasis on the survival of its characters, Under the Dome simply wasn’t as captivating as Lost . Maybe that’s because its story was adapted from a Stephen King story rather than being original like Lost , but it simply couldn’t capture lightning in the same way. 3) FlashForward (ABC, 2009-2010) There are several sci-fi TV shows that deserved another season , but few stand out as strongly as FlashForward . Its premise was relatively simple: a mysterious event causes the world’s population to get a two-minute glimpse six months into the future. Its story focused on a number of characters attempting to unravel the mysteries surrounding this event, as well as understand the future they saw during that two-minute window. In fairness, FlashForward could easily have been the new Lost . Its unique premise featured a great deal of mystery and suspense, and it was gripping from its very first scene. As the showrunners had no idea it was being cancelled, it’s an example of a TV show that ended on an annoying cliffhanger , with the season one finale setting up an exciting follow-up that never came. Had FlashForward continued, it could have reached the same heights as Lost while also fitting into the same niche, but it simply wasn’t to be. 2) Manifest (NBC, 2018-2021 & Netflix, 2022-2023) An incredibly recent example of a show that came close to filling Lost ‘s shoes, Manifest was almost there when it came to global success. First airing in 2018 on NBC, Manifest ran for three seasons before being cancelled, only to be picked up by Netflix for a fourth and final season. Its story follows the passengers and crew of an airliner who suddenly reappear more than five years after their plane went missing. In terms of the overall thrust of its story, Manifest was clearly emulating Lost . The problem with that is that Lost ‘s countless twists led audiences to grow somewhat tired of TV shows that take too many turns , and Manifest couldn’t hit the same viewership figures as the show it evoked. Shohreh Aghdashloo, Aya Cash, Madelyn Cline, Mike Colter, Colman Domingo, Tom Ellis, Courtney Ford, Tiffany Haddish, Sam Heughan, Maddison Jaizani, Lennie James, Martin Kove, Javicia Leslie, Leah Lewis, Caity Lotz, Ralph Macchio, Kennedy McMann, Elizabeth Mitchell, Lindsey Morgan, Bob Morley, Genevieve Padalecki, Jared Padalecki, Brandon Routh, Chase Stokes, Eliza Taylor, Gina Torres, Alan Tudyk, and William Zabka, will all serve as presenters during the special ceremony, which will air on The CW Network on Sunday, January 10, 2021 (8:00-10:00pm ET/PT) and will stream the next day for free on The CW App and cwtv.com. “We know that the Super Awards are in the best hands with Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the helm,” said Critics Choice Association CEO Joey Berlin. “They bring with them an unparalleled knowledge of and enthusiasm for these sometimes underappreciated genres that we know fans and viewers will love. They are joined by a stellar line-up of fan favorites who will be on hand to support their ‘Super’ colleagues and help showcase the very best in popular entertainment.” The Critics Choice Association will also present the Legacy Award to the “Star Trek” franchise, recognizing the cultural impact it has had across multiple decades while continuing to appeal to and grow its loyal fanbase with new stories and characters. “Star Trek” icon Patrick Stewart , and “Star Trek: Discovery” trailblazer Sonequa Martin-Green will personally accept this special honor, which comes as the franchise celebrates its 55 th anniversary. See also Critics Choice Association to Honor Harrison Ford Hulu and NEON’s “Palm Springs” leads this year’s film nominees, with a total of five including Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Andy Samberg, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie and Best Villain in a Movie for J.K. Simmons, and Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Cristin Milioti. Several films followed close behind with four nominations including “Birds of Prey” (Warner Bros.), “Freaky” (Universal), “Onward” (Disney+), “Sonic the Hedgehog” (Paramount), “The Hunt” (Universal), “The Old Guard” (Netflix), and “The Willoughbys” (Netflix). “Lovecraft Country” (HBO) received the most television nominations, with a total of six possible wins, including Best Horror Series, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Jonathan Majors, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Michael K. Williams, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Wunmi Mosaku, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Jurnee Smollett, and Best Villain in a Series for Abbey Lee. Amazon’s “The Boys” received five nominations including Best Superhero/Comic Book Series, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series and Best Villain in a Series for Antony Starr, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Karl Urban, and Best Actress in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Aya Cash. She can currently be seen on Syfy’s “The Great Debate” and in Disney’s “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” playing herself. She is also an accomplished television writer with credits at Netflix and HBO Max. But the seven-season series is about to leave streaming, and no one yet knows where it will move to. While the 20th Century was arguably the golden age for sci-fi TV, people tend to forget how good the 2010s were. Stranger Things , Westworld , Dark , The Expanse , Black Mirror , The Mandalorian , Love, Death + Robots , and the criminally underrated Legion all debuted during that decade. But ask any CW binge-watcher which sci-fi series dominated the 2010s, and they\'ll undoubtedly answer The 100 . Unfortunately, like the human survivors abandoning The Ark, The 100 is about to leave Netflix. The show will vacate Netflix\'s streaming library on December 18. That\'s right, all seven seasons of The 100 will no longer stream on Netflix from December. The show\'s removal from Netflix comes alongside the streamer\'s culling of several popular shows from its content library. As well as The 100 , Supernatural and Arrow (another CW hit) will also leave Netflix in December. The 100 is based on the young adult sci-fi series of the same name written by Kass Morgan. The four books in the series were turned into a seven-season show on The CW, which debuted in 2014 and ran until 2020. The story itself takes place almost a century after nuclear war has destroyed the Earth. The few surviving humans fled to outer space on a giant self-sufficient station known as The Ark. But when The Ark begins to shut down, 100 juveniles are sent down to Earth to see if it is safe to return. The official synopsis reads: "When nuclear Armageddon destroys civilization on Earth, the only survivors are those on the 12 international space stations in orbit at the time. Three generations later, the 4,000 survivors living on a space ark of linked stations see their resources dwindle and face Draconian measures established to ensure humanity\'s future. Desperately looking for a solution, the ark\'s leaders send 100 juvenile prisoners back to the planet to test its habitability. Having always lived in space, the exiles find the planet fascinating and terrifying, but with the fate of the human race in their hands, they must forge a path into the unknown." \'The 100\' Divided Critics & Audiences During Its Run Eliza Taylor in the 100. The CW Like many of The CW\'s best shows, The 100 got off to a tremendous start. Season 1 received decent reviews from both critics and audiences, holding a 76% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a stronger audience score of 78%. Season 2 was ever more well received, earning a prestigious 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a strong audience score of 87%. "Best show on TV. I liked The Black List and Arrow before, but this one is far better. Still like the others, but this one is well written and keeps you guessing," wrote one user after watching the second season. The 100 experienced a strange phenomenon in its later seasons. Seasons 5, 6, and 7 are all 100% rated on Rotten Tomatoes from critics\' reviews. However, audiences slowly fell off with the final seasons. Season 7, which was released in May 2020, holds a measly audience score of just 42%, compared to its perfect critics\' rating. Following the survivors of a plane crash as they uncover various mysteries on a desert island, Lost captivated audiences around the world almost instantly. Sadly, Lost became an example of a great TV show that was terrible by the end , but despite its disappointing finale, the ABC show outlived even its own massive success. It is often credited with revolutionizing the format of modern television, focusing on wider story arcs rather than dedicating itself to an episodic format. After running for three seasons across 34 episodes, Travelers was prematurely canceled. Travelers could easily have become the new Lost , had it found a way to reach a wider audience. For all its narrative potential and mysterious plot developments, Travelers simply didn’t land high enough viewership to reach the levels of popularity enjoyed by Lost . As great as the show could have been, its ratings also led to its cancellation, dooming it to never quite reach its full potential. 4) Under the Dome (CBS, 2013-2015) Although there are many great Stephen King movies , there aren’t as many noteworthy TV shows based on the iconic author’s works. Its story focused on a number of characters attempting to unravel the mysteries surrounding this event, as well as understand the future they saw during that two-minute window. Shohreh Aghdashloo, Aya Cash, Madelyn Cline, Mike Colter, Colman Domingo, Tom Ellis, Courtney Ford, Tiffany Haddish, Sam Heughan, Maddison Jaizani, Lennie James, Martin Kove, Javicia Leslie, Leah Lewis, Caity Lotz, Ralph Macchio, Kennedy McMann, Elizabeth Mitchell, Lindsey Morgan, Bob Morley, Genevieve Padalecki, Jared Padalecki, Brandon Routh, Chase Stokes, Eliza Taylor, Gina Torres, Alan Tudyk, and William Zabka, will all serve as presenters during the special ceremony, which will air on The CW Network on Sunday, January 10, 2021 (8:00-10:00pm ET/PT) and will stream the next day for free on The CW App and cwtv.com. “We know that the Super Awards are in the best hands with Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the helm,” said Critics Choice Association CEO Joey Berlin. “They bring with them an unparalleled knowledge of and enthusiasm for these sometimes underappreciated genres that we know fans and viewers will love. They are joined by a stellar line-up of fan favorites who will be on hand to support their ‘Super’ colleagues and help showcase the very best in popular entertainment.” The Critics Choice Association will also present the Legacy Award to the “Star Trek” franchise, recognizing the cultural impact it has had across multiple decades while continuing to appeal to and grow its loyal fanbase with new stories and characters. “Star Trek” icon Patrick Stewart , and “Star Trek: Discovery” trailblazer Sonequa Martin-Green will personally accept this special honor, which comes as the franchise celebrates its 55 th anniversary. See also Critics Choice Association to Honor Harrison Ford Hulu and NEON’s “Palm Springs” leads this year’s film nominees, with a total of five including Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Andy Samberg, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie and Best Villain in a Movie for J.K. Simmons, and Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Cristin Milioti. Several films followed close behind with four nominations including “Birds of Prey” (Warner Bros.), “Freaky” (Universal), “Onward” (Disney+), “Sonic the Hedgehog” (Paramount), “The Hunt” (Universal), “The Old Guard” (Netflix), and “The Willoughbys” (Netflix). “Lovecraft Country” (HBO) received the most television nominations, with a total of six possible wins, including Best Horror Series, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Jonathan Majors, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Michael K. Williams, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Wunmi Mosaku, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Jurnee Smollett, and Best Villain in a Series for Abbey Lee. Amazon’s “The Boys” received five nominations including Best Superhero/Comic Book Series, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series and Best Villain in a Series for Antony Starr, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Karl Urban, and Best Actress in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Aya Cash. For the full list of nominees, and additional information, visit: https://www.criticschoice.com/critics-choice-super-awards/ Kevin Smith has been saying silly cinematic shit since 1994’s “Clerks.” 2021 marks the 27 th year since the last time he had a real job. She can currently be seen on Syfy’s “The Great Debate” and in Disney’s “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” playing herself. She is also an accomplished television writer with credits at Netflix and HBO Max. Dumfries Edinburgh Glenrothes Perth Scotland By Sandra Dick Journalist @sandradick Share 0 Comments Families of Darcy McGuire (left), Kayden Trayner (top right pictured with siblings) and Holly Clarke have launched children's hospice CHAS's Christmas 2025 campaign (Image: CHAS) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A little girl with dreams of one last Christmas, a teenager living with a cruel illness and devastated parents who surrounded their daughter with love as they said their last farewells. They are the faces at the forefront of a powerful new campaign being launched this week by CHAS - Children’s Hospices Across Scotland. The Christmas That Couldn’t Wait Appeal aims to bring moments of comfort and joy to children with life-shortening conditions and support for their families at times when they need it most. The charity , which runs two hospices, Rachel House in Kinross and Robin House in Balloch , provides expert medical, nursing, and social work care for families facing the most difficult times of their lives. Darcy McGuire at CHAS's Rachel House (Image: CHAS) The appeal’s name was inspired by eight-year-old Darcy McGuire from Glenrothes, who was diagnosed in 2018 with Chordoma, a one-in-20-million rare cancer usually found in older adults. Her condition deteriorated rapidly. By November 2019, and aware that her time was running out, Rachel House staff brought the festive magic forward to give her and her family a final Christmas together. Her mum, Carol, says the hospice provided a precious time for them to enjoy making final memories. “She said, ‘Mum, I’m not going to be here at Christmas’,” says Carol. “I said, ‘You thought that at your birthday, and you ended up having two birthdays. Let’s just spoil you and have two Christmases’.” Her room was decorated with its own Christmas tree, glitter and decorations, and a party was held with festive food and gifts. Darcy McGuire, who had one last Christmas arranged by CHAS, with her mum Carol (Image: CHAS) Carol adds: “I knew that day was her last Christmas.” Darcy’s condition went downhill quickly, and she died on 15 December that year. Her funeral was held on Christmas Eve. Six years on, the family still set a place for her at the Christmas table and even visit Rachel House to relive happy family moments. As well as giving the family a last Christmas together, the hospice provided important care to keep Darcy comfortable and ease her anxiety. Read more: Trustees’ Week shines light on unsung heroes of Scotland’s charities More than £18,000 raised for family of Olivia Grace Edwards Baby loss support service 'may have to turn people away' “She was scared about leaving me and her dad,” recalls Carol. “We had a final honest conversation. I told her, ‘We will all be okay. We’ll remember you. We’ll be alright.’ And that was enough for her. She stopped fighting after that.” In Dumfries, Stevi Robertson also knows the value of the hospice charity’s support as it cared for her daughter Holly during the last year of her life. Holly received care at Robin House in Balloch (Image: CHAS) Holly, a twin, had been starved of oxygen for 15 minutes at birth leaving her with the brain injury spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy with epilepsy. The family were warned she might not survive beyond her second birthday and would not be able to walk, talk or eat. Holly was eight when her condition deteriorated in 2019. Her family made their first visit to Robin House in Balloch that December for palliative respite care. It became a ‘home from home’ and even when lockdown restrictions arrived, the hospice provided online support for the family and Holly’s siblings, and made arrangements for a community hospital team to provide nursing care. As the end grew closer, it helped the family take Holly to the beach – her ‘happy place’. “It took a lot of effort and a lot of drugs, but we got her there. The sun shone on her cheeks, and she loved it,” adds Stevi. Holly was cared for at CHAS's Robin House, Balloch (Image: CHAS) Holly died on 29 October, 2020, with her mum holding her hand and her favourite Frozen songs playing in the background. It was ‘good death’ that has brought the family comfort, says Stevi. “She was surrounded by her family and so much love,” she adds. “We were heartbroken but so grateful to have CHAS’s support. “The most important thing they provided for us was a good death for our beautiful daughter… a death with no regrets. “Thanks to CHAS we knew that Holly wasn’t in pain when she died and she wasn’t suffering and when the time came for her to slip away, we knew she was comfortable. “We will always be grateful to CHAS for the part they played in that and for being there for us all as a family.” As well as integrated palliative and end of life care, the hospice charity provides important support for young people with a range of life-shortening conditions and aiding every family member affected emotionally, clinically, and practically. While for families facing the expense of caring for children with complex needs, there is also vital financial guidance. Valerie Trayner, mum to Kayden, 17, who has Juvenile Batten Disease, recently benefited from advice from the Financial Wellbeing and Energy Advice (FWEA) service, which has helped save families over £2m over the past two years. “When you have a child with complex needs who relies on a lot of electrical equipment such as a feeding pump and an electric bed and an overhead hoist, costs add up,” says Valerie, from Edinburgh . Valerie Trayner with Kayden who has Juvenile Batten Disease (Image: CHAS) “The FWEA team have helped me in many ways – by going through our family finances, suggesting ways in which savings could be made and informing us about funding and benefits we could apply – many of which we did not even realise we were entitled to. “Thanks to the support we are now in a much more comfortable position financially which has relieved a lot of stress and means we can look forward to Christmas this year.” CHAS CEO Rami Okasha says: “There are thousands of families across Scotland having to deal with the unthinkable reality that their child may die young. “CHAS provides expert medical, nursing, and social work care for families facing the most difficult times of their lives. Valerie Trayner says she has received advice from CHAS to help with costs involved in Kayden's care (Image: CHAS) “We remain utterly focused on being there for families at every stage of their palliative care journeys, from the moment a parent learns their child is seriously ill and may die young, helping them live well, and providing dignified end-of-life care. “CHAS provides expert medical, nursing, and social work care for families facing the most difficult times of their lives. “We’re seeing more people needing urgent support and, without immediate action, we simply won’t be able to meet this growing demand. “We know we can’t reach everyone who needs us without the kindness and generosity of our supporters, so we are asking the Scottish public for their help by donating to our Christmas appeal.” To donate to CHAS’s The Christmas That Couldn’t Wait Appeal visit: www.chas.org.uk/appeal CHAS Charity Children's Hospices Around Scotland Children's Health Christmas Charity Health People Dumbarton Dumfries Edinburgh Glenrothes Perth Scotland Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... Barbara (Natasha Liu Bordizzo) is a fashion influencer who champions #girlpower online but prefers parties over protests. While Elise (Lydia West) is an awkward English exchange student determined to reinvent herself as a one-woman Pussy Riot, but is terrified of getting in trouble. After a chance meeting in art class and a shared frustration with the men in their lives, they form an unlikely alliance and spearhead a ‘Kill All Men’ art project. Drunk as skunks in the dead of night, the girls deface a statue of the university’s male founder in the quadrangle. By morning, the campus’s star athlete is found murdered and displayed at the foot of their political statement. < Barbara and Elise must urgently erase all evidence connecting them to the crime as Detective Shepherd (Liv Hewson) is hot on their heels. As gender tensions escalate on campus with a growing male body count, the girls are forced to uncover the real culprit, all whilst attempting to stop the gender riot they unintentionally created before it turns into a full-blown gender war. He Had It Coming was created and written by Gretel Vella and Craig Anderson with Emme Hoy ( Renegade Nell ), Belinda King ( Wellmania ), Nick Coyle ( Bump ) and Hannah Samuel ( The Heights ) serving as writers. Thursday 30 October 2025 20:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 3:46 \'They have scandal after scandal\' Why you can trust Sky News Kemi Badenoch has said hacking into Harriet Harman\'s website when she was younger is "not the same" as Rachel Reeves failing to get a £900 rental licence for her home. The Tory leader, who has called for the chancellor to go for breaking the law, told Sky News\' deputy political editor Sam Coates she was not an MP in 2008 when she got into Labour peer Baroness Harman\'s website and changed it so it was pro-Conservative. Politics latest: Reeves told she has to go after breaking law Hacking into websites is a criminal offence and can be punishable with a fine or up to a two-year prison sentence for minor offences, or life imprisonment for the most serious. Asked if she had ever broken the law, Ms Badenoch said: "I don\'t believe that I have, but if I had done so, if I had done so when I was in government, then I would have been sacked or I would have been forced to resign." But reminded of her hacking episode, she said: "This was something I did in my 20s. "We\'re not talking about something that Rachel Reeves did in her 20s, we\'re talking about something she\'s doing as chancellor, after she became chancellor. "It is not the same thing at all." For the first time, Children’s Hospices Across Scotland (CHAS) has transformed the gardens at Robin House into an accessible pumpkin patch. The colourful patch was created by the dedicated gardening and activities teams at the children’s hospice, with pumpkins, craft materials and Halloween-themed treats donated by Aldi Scotland. Families enjoyed picking pumpkins, creating spooky decorations, painting and biscuit decorating, and taking part in fun seasonal activities designed to be inclusive for everyone. In previous years, Robin House families visited local farms to pick pumpkins, but wet weather and uneven ground made it difficult for some children to take part. Daniel and family enjoying the CHAS pumpkin patch (Image: Supplied) Determined to ensure every child could enjoy the same fun, the team brought the experience to them, decorating the hospice gardens with hay bales, autumn leaves and bright orange pumpkins. Maggie Brown, CHAS Robin House gardener, said: “I am so proud of our brilliant gardening team at Robin House for helping to bring this special pumpkin patch to the hospice gardens for the first time, making it fully accessible for all children and families. “We wanted every child to feel the joy of picking their own pumpkin and we are so grateful to Aldi Scotland for kindly donating all 60 of the pumpkins along with Halloween crafts, fun painting kits and biscuit decorating bags. “The children joined a scavenger hunt organised by our brilliant activities team, and also enjoyed spooky stories and an and arts and crafts workshop. Creating this little patch of autumn magic right here at Robin House has been a labour of love but the smiles from the children say it all.” Alison Ringrose, activities facilitator at Robin House, added: “All of the children and young people who visited the patch with their families said how amazing it was. Maggie and her garden volunteers worked so hard to make the pumpkin patch special and fully accessible for everyone.” Robin House gardener Maggie Brown and the CHAS team (Image: Supplied) The pumpkin patch formed part of a week-long celebration of Halloween at Robin House, where families also enjoyed a spooky sing-along, monster biscuit-making workshop, sensory play and fancy dress. These activities helped create even more seasonal magic for children staying at the hospice, ensuring every moment was filled with laughter and creativity. Continuing the Halloween giving, Aldi Scotland also turned its Renfrew store into a pop-up pumpkin patch for families in the area to enjoy, offering visitors the chance to decorate pumpkins, take part in crafts and make a small donation to CHAS. The event raised £120 to help fund the charity’s vital work across Scotland. Graham Nicolson, group buying director at Aldi Scotland, said: “CHAS provides an incredible lifeline for families across Scotland, and we were proud to support the team at Robin House in creating such a magical and inclusive experience. Seeing the joy it brought to children and their families perfectly captures the spirit of CHAS and the difference it makes every day.” CHAS supports more than 500 children with life-shortening conditions and their families each year, providing palliative, respite and end-of-life care at Rachel House in Kinross, Robin House in Balloch, and through CHAS at Home services across Scotland. For more information about CHAS and how to support its work, visit www.chas.org.uk . Image via Prime Video By Tyler B. Searle Published Nov 17, 2025 Born with Autism (formerly classified as Asperger syndrome), Tyler B. Searle has been obsessed with storytelling since he was old enough to speak. He gravitated towards fairy tales, mythology, the fantasy genre, and animated movies and shows aimed at family audiences. When not writing, Tyler enjoys watching more cartoons and reading fantasy books in his home in Ontario, Canada. Sign in to your Collider account follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap In 2015, a group of voice actors sat down together and uploaded their game of Dungeons & Dragons to the internet. It marked the beginning of Critical Role, which has since blossomed into a massive franchise comprising three complete D&D games (and a fourth, which began in 2025) and various spinoffs. In 2022, they partnered with Amazon to release The Legend of Vox Machina , an animated series based on Critical Role\'s first D&D game, with each player returning to voice their character, and Dungeon Master Matthew Mercer voicing a wide array of side-characters and villains. The success of the show led to four seasons and a spinoff, The Mighty Nein , which premieres later this week. Given that the show is adapting 115 episodes between 3 and 6 hours long on average, a lot of changes had to be made in this adaptation. Some are very big and result in major alterations to the flow of events, for better or for worse. This list will discuss the biggest differences between Critical Role\'s first campaign and The Legend of Vox Machina , highlighting how they separate both projects and whether the changes were effective or not. Kraghammer Vax\'ildan battles an Onlooker Image via Prime Video The Legend of Vox Machina begins with an early arc of the campaign that was played before they started streaming, where the team faced off against the Blue Dragon, Brimscythe ( David Tennant ), before jumping into the Briarwood Arc. However, the live-play had several more arcs before the Briarwoods showed up, with the first ones audiences got to watch taking place around the dwarven citadel of Kraghammer. Vox Machina got involved in a deadly adventure through the Underdark, where they faced armies of evil dwarves called Duergar, brain-eating Mind Flayers, and a powerful Beholder who had merged itself with a demonic artifact. The most likely reason for Kraghammer\'s omission is that it centered around Beholders and Mind Flayers , two of Dungeons & Dragons\' most iconic and trademarked creatures. While the adventures in the Underdark were fun and introduced memorable characters, like the rogue Mind Flayer Clarota, it would have been a nightmare to re-tweak everything to work around copyright , and it would delay what many people consider the best arc in Campaign 1. The main casualty of this arc\'s drop is that this was when Lady Kima ( Stephanie Beatriz ) was introduced to the story, and became fireforged friends with Vox Machina, something that doesn\'t happen until midway through Season 2 in the show. Thordak\'s Eggs A dragon egg sitting in a nest of lava Image via Prime Video After his Chroma Conclave conquers the capital city of Emon, Thordak ( Lance Reddick ) transforms the city into a volcanic hellscape while the citizens deliver all their treasure to him. Thanks to the Soul Anchor embedded in his chest, Thordak undergoes a transformation that increases his size, strength and gives him the ability to reproduce asexually. As his mind degrades, Thordak commits himself to protecting the eggs so that his progeny can hatch and claim the world for dragonkind. In the live play, Vox Machina didn\'t learn of the eggs until after Thordak was killed , and they were swiftly dealt with before any could hatch. The show had the characters learn about the eggs at the beginning of Season 3 to stress the importance of getting as much power as possible. The eggs are also allowed to hatch, meaning that we get to see Vox Machina hold their own against an army of baby dragons the size of ponies, which is just as cool as it sounds. Missing Vestiges of Divergence Scanlan holds Mythcarver Image via Prime Video To defeat the Chroma Conclave, Vox Machina is told of powerful artifacts created by the gods called the Vestiges of Divergence. Unfortunately, each Vestige is guarded by a fierce guardian, including a mighty sphynx who has never felt pain and an archfey from the Fey Realm corrupted by heartbreak and jealousy. Unfortunately, they\'re not alone in the hunt, as the black dragon member of the conclave, Umbrasyl (Matthew Mercer), also wants the Vestiges to use their power for himself. Every member of Vox Machina got a Vestige in the live play , but the show cuts out three , claimed by Keyleth ( Marishia Ray ), Percy ( Taliesin Jaffe ), and Vax\'ildan ( Liam O\'Brien ). Keyleth\'s, called the Spire of Conflux, is a magic staff that had to be retrieved from the belly of a demon named Yenk (Matthew Mercer), while Percy\'s is Cabal\'s Ruin, a magic cloak that can absorb magic. Vax at least gets to keep his first Vestige, the Deathwalker\'s Ward, but he also claimed Whisper, a dagger that allows its wielder to teleport when thrown and frighten those it strikes. A Bard\'s Lament Scanland from the Legend of Vox Machina Image via Prime Video The gnome bard, Scanlan Shorthalt ( Sam Reigel ), is first introduced as the group\'s comic relief, who always looks for an excuse to make a raunchy joke. Season 2 sees him begin to re-evaluate things when he learns that he has a daughter, Kaylie ( Aisling Franciosi ). Their relationship is understandably rocky at first, but by the end of Season 3, Scanlan decides to travel with her when Vox Machina decides to temporarily disband following the defeat of the Chroma Conclave. Scanlan\'s departure was far from a happy goodbye in the live play . Rather, it was a messy argument that was the culmination of a long arc of Scanlan spiraling into depression and drug use , made even worse because his friends let Kaylie see his dead body (smeared with pudding and wearing a dress) during a resurrection ritual, not knowing that Scanlan had promised Kaylie that he wouldn\'t die on his quest. It makes sense to end the season on a happy note (especially since they didn\'t know if they would get a 4th season), but it would have been awesome to see the actors act out this scene with polish, especially when Scanlan calls out the rest of Vox Machina for not asking about his past. Anna Ripley Anna Ripley wearing a hood and looking behind a rock Image via Prime Video Dr. Anna Ripley ( Kelly Hu ) worked alongside the Briarwoods to kill the De Rolo family and take over the city of Whitestone. She used her brilliant mind to help produce an acidic compound to refine a magic ore called residuum, and also tortured Percy, the last son of the De Rolos. Once her work was finished, Ripley was betrayed by the Briarwoods and locked in prison, but she escaped with help from Vox Machina and came back later to cause trouble during their hunt for the Vestiges of Divergence. For the most part, Ripley follows the same plot as her live show counterpart, but the show gives her more screentime that greatly fleshes out her character . Her backstory sees her lose her family to powerful mages, which helps to explain why she is so committed to the mass production of firearms, and sets her as an even greater foil to Percy. She\'s also given a bit of a manipulative streak, as she gets in good with Umbrasyl to begin the hunt for the Vestiges, and later tells Thordak about Whitestone, so his children can feed on its people. Raishan Raishan in her draconic form Image via Amazon Prime Video Thordak might be the leader of the Chroma Conclave, but the real brains behind the alliance is the green dragon Raishan ( Cree Summer ). She formed the conclave for Thordak and freed him from the Fire Plane in exchange for his knowledge of a cure to the druidic disease that is slowly killing her, but he withheld the information. Thus, she turns to Vox Machina for revenge, though it is a very shaky alliance, especially because of Raishan and Keyleth\'s mutual hatred. Summer does a great job voicing Raishan, and overall, she hits the same story beats as her original self, but the show\'s take on Raishan feels like a less effective antagonist . Live play Raishan was not only intelligent and cunning, but a wizard who had access to some of the strongest spells, which she used to augment her natural draconic strength and kill several members of Vox Machina across two fights. Show Raishan, meanwhile, feels much weaker because she\'s always in human form , and only fights Vox Machina once when she possesses Thordak\'s corpse. This approach not only makes the fight feel like Thordak 2.0 (especially since Raishan barely casts any magic), but she\'s pretty much defeated solely by Keyleth, which makes her feel like quite a letdown, especially since this fight in the live play still had Keyleth be the key member thanks to a game-changing Feeblemind spell. Percy\'s Death Image via Prime Video The existence of resurrection magic can lead to a problem in stories, as it risks making death feel cheap if the characters can just be easily brought back to life. This feeling was pretty rampant in the live play, with each member of Vox Machina dying at least once, so the show kept things limited to allow for the best deaths from the live play to hit with maximum emotional weight. Yet nobody was expecting Percy\'s death at the hands of Anna Ripley to wind up like it did. While in the live play, Percy was resurrected relatively quickly; the show plays Percy\'s death as if there\'s no bringing him back , complete with a funeral and intense grief among the surviving members of Vox Machina. It\'s only when Vax learns that Percy\'s soul was claimed by the demon Orthax (Matthew Mercer), who previously made a deal with Percy to help him create his first gun, that they can perform a ritual to allow Vax into Orthax\'s realm. An intense battle between Vax and Orthax over Percy\'s soul ensues, with Vex\'ahlia ( Laura Bailey ) delivering one of the best lines of the show to help bring him home. Kashaw and Zahra Zara and Kashaw standing in a snowy forest Image via Prime Video Critical Role often invited their fellow voice actors to appear as guest characters for an episode or two. Some of the best-received characters were the human cleric, Kashaw ( Will Friedle ), and the tiefling warlock, Zahra ( Mary Elizabeth McGlynn ), who first teamed up with Vox Machina to hunt monsters for a guild called The Slayer\'s Take. They rejoined Vox Machina several times, so it was natural to see them appear as recurring characters in the show. While Zahra and Kashaw very quickly form a friendship with Vox Machina in the live play, their show counterparts are far more antagonistic , with Zahra even unleashing the Onlooker so they can steal the Deathwalker\'s Ward, forcing Vax to save them when it goes on a rampage. The biggest change came during the battle against Thordak, where Kashaw is killed, leaving Zahra distraught. This change adds more stakes to the battle against such a mighty dragon , and to deny Vox Machina access to his resurrection abilities when it was time to bring Percy back. With Season 4 greenlit, we\'ll have to wait and see how his death with affect Zahra\'s role during the final arc. The Journey to Hell Image via Prime Video The quest to get Pike Trickfoot\'s ( Ashley Johnson ) Vestige, the Plate of the Dawnmartyr, is drastically different between the two mediums . In the live play, they traveled to the Plane of Fire, had to navigate a city where one slip up could see them enslaved , and battled a deadly Pit Fiend to get the Vestige from a Fire Giant. In the show, the Plate is instead located in hell, guarded by a powerful demon named Zerxus ( Luis Carazo ), who challenges Pike to a card game that leaves her questioning her faith in her goddess. Vox Machina did go to hell in the live play, but it was to kill a Rakshasa named Hotis, who had sworn vengeance against Vax and nearly killed him by taking the form of their sorcerer friend, Shaun Gilmore ( Sunil Malhotra ). The show instead turns Hotis into a cameo in Season 1 when the group is talking about their strangest kills. Zerxus is also a character from a spinoff campaign, Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, and his backstory to Pike directly references that campaign, making it an example of Critical Role using the show to bridge their various projects . Tiberius Stormwind Image via Prime Video During the early days of the campaign, Vox Machina had an eighth member: a red dragonborn sorcerer named Tiberius Stormwind ( Orion Acaba ), from the floating isles of Draconia. He accompanied the group while searching for missing Draconian artifacts, but left them shortly after their first battle with the Briarwoods. When Vox Machina later went to Draconia to hunt the white dragon Vorugal (Liam O\'Brien), they found Tiberius\' frozen body, indicating that he died trying to defend his city from the Fridgid Doom. The reason for Tiberius\' sudden departure was due to Acaba\'s actions, both on and off camera . It\'s a shame because Tiberius was a pretty fun character thanks to his bumbling mage archetype, but the longer those early episodes went on, the more of Acaba\'s habits seeped into the character. The show did include a dragonborn sorcerer named Dohla ( Rachel House ), a former ally of Kima and Allura ( Indira Varma )—the latter of whom Tiberius also had a crush on—who betrays them due to jealousy before being unceremoniously killed by Vorugal. It\'s especially strange because Dohla, like Tiberius, died heroically in the live play, but in combining the two characters, the show chose to only focus on the negative traits, making her a superfluous villain and robbing Vox Machina of a heroic dragonborn ally. It is regrettable that information provided on successive days has generated confusion, but I find no evidence of bad faith.” Advertisement Despite being cleared by Magnus, Reeves still faces the possibility of being ordered to hand back more than £41,000 that her tenants have paid in rent. She could also face a civil fine of up to £30,000 and be added to the national “rogue landlord” database. Chris Bryant, the trade minister, said the chancellor “hadn’t completely remembered” the facts around letting out her home and that Reeves and her husband would be “kicking themselves”. He told Times Radio: “They went to a letting agency, as anybody else would do, and the letting agency said, ‘Look, you’ve got to get a licence, but we’ll sort all of that out for you’. “Now it turns out that she and her husband hadn’t completely remembered all of those facts about the interaction with the agency when they first spoke to the prime minister about it. And I’m sure Rachel and her husband are absolutely kicking themselves about it.” Bryant accused the Times Radio presenter Calum Macdonald of acting like “the judge and jury and hanging executioner” over his questions on Reeves. Advertisement He told Sky News: “It would be better, obviously, if they found those emails right at the beginning.” The Conservatives called on Starmer to start a “proper investigation” into the case, which Kemi Badenoch said “stinks”. The Tory leader added: “The prime minister needs to stop trying to cover this up, order a full investigation and, if Reeves has broken the law, grow a backbone and sack her.” Kemi Badenoch called for Reeves to be sacked if she broke the law It emerged late on Wednesday that Reeves had been renting out her four-bedroom property through a letting agency for £3,200 a month since September last year, when she moved her family into Downing Street. Southwark council requires private landlords to obtain a “selective” licence, costing £900, if their property is situated in certain areas, which are listed clearly on its website. Reeves endorsed plans for a property rental licensing scheme in her Leeds constituency days before it was revealed she had flouted the rules herself. Advertisement The chancellor initially claimed in a letter to Starmer that “regrettably” she and her husband, Nick Joicey, “were not aware that a licence was necessary” and “did not obtain [one] before letting the property out”. She said that it had been an “inadvertent mistake”, adding: “As soon as it was brought to my attention, we took immediate action and applied for the licence.” Nick Joicey NIGEL HOWARD MEDIA However, less than 24 hours later Reeves wrote again to Starmer to admit she had “found” emails with the couple’s letting agent, Harvey & Wheeler, which showed that they had been informed. The agent apologised to the chancellor yesterday for having offered to apply for a licence but failing to do so in an “oversight”. • The Times view: Rachel Reeves has been trapped by the red tape she championed The emails revealed conversations between Joicey, a former civil servant, and the agent in which the licence was mentioned seven times. Holly Clarke have launched children's hospice CHAS's Christmas 2025 campaign (Image: CHAS) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A little girl with dreams of one last Christmas, a teenager living with a cruel illness and devastated parents who surrounded their daughter with love as they said their last farewells. They are the faces at the forefront of a powerful new campaign being launched this week by CHAS - Children’s Hospices Across Scotland. The Christmas That Couldn’t Wait Appeal aims to bring moments of comfort and joy to children with life-shortening conditions and support for their families at times when they need it most. The charity , which runs two hospices, Rachel House in Kinross and Robin House in Balloch , provides expert medical, nursing, and social work care for families facing the most difficult times of their lives. Darcy McGuire at CHAS's Rachel House (Image: CHAS) The appeal’s name was inspired by eight-year-old Darcy McGuire from Glenrothes, who was diagnosed in 2018 with Chordoma, a one-in-20-million rare cancer usually found in older adults. Her condition deteriorated rapidly. By November 2019, and aware that her time was running out, Rachel House staff brought the festive magic forward to give her and her family a final Christmas together. Her mum, Carol, says the hospice provided a precious time for them to enjoy making final memories. “She said, ‘Mum, I’m not going to be here at Christmas’,” says Carol. “I said, ‘You thought that at your birthday, and you ended up having two birthdays. Let’s just spoil you and have two Christmases’.” Her room was decorated with its own Christmas tree, glitter and decorations, and a party was held with festive food and gifts. Darcy McGuire, who had one last Christmas arranged by CHAS, with her mum Carol (Image: CHAS) Carol adds: “I knew that day was her last Christmas.” Darcy’s condition went downhill quickly, and she died on 15 December that year. Her funeral was held on Christmas Eve. Six years on, the family still set a place for her at the Christmas table and even visit Rachel House to relive happy family moments. As well as giving the family a last Christmas together, the hospice provided important care to keep Darcy comfortable and ease her anxiety. Read more: Trustees’ Week shines light on unsung heroes of Scotland’s charities More than £18,000 raised for family of Olivia Grace Edwards Baby loss support service 'may have to turn people away' “She was scared about leaving me and her dad,” recalls Carol. “We had a final honest conversation. I told her, ‘We will all be okay. We’ll remember you. We’ll be alright.’ And that was enough for her. She stopped fighting after that.” In Dumfries, Stevi Robertson also knows the value of the hospice charity’s support as it cared for her daughter Holly during the last year of her life. Holly received care at Robin House in Balloch (Image: CHAS) Holly, a twin, had been starved of oxygen for 15 minutes at birth leaving her with the brain injury spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy with epilepsy. The family were warned she might not survive beyond her second birthday and would not be able to walk, talk or eat. Holly was eight when her condition deteriorated in 2019. Her family made their first visit to Robin House in Balloch that December for palliative respite care. It became a ‘home from home’ and even when lockdown restrictions arrived, the hospice provided online support for the family and Holly’s siblings, and made arrangements for a community hospital team to provide nursing care. As the end grew closer, it helped the family take Holly to the beach – her ‘happy place’. “It took a lot of effort and a lot of drugs, but we got her there. The sun shone on her cheeks, and she loved it,” adds Stevi. Holly was cared for at CHAS's Robin House, Balloch (Image: CHAS) Holly died on 29 October, 2020, with her mum holding her hand and her favourite Frozen songs playing in the background. It was ‘good death’ that has brought the family comfort, says Stevi. “She was surrounded by her family and so much love,” she adds. “We were heartbroken but so grateful to have CHAS’s support. “The most important thing they provided for us was a good death for our beautiful daughter… a death with no regrets. “Thanks to CHAS we knew that Holly wasn’t in pain when she died and she wasn’t suffering and when the time came for her to slip away, we knew she was comfortable. “We will always be grateful to CHAS for the part they played in that and for being there for us all as a family.” As well as integrated palliative and end of life care, the hospice charity provides important support for young people with a range of life-shortening conditions and aiding every family member affected emotionally, clinically, and practically. While for families facing the expense of caring for children with complex needs, there is also vital financial guidance. Valerie Trayner, mum to Kayden, 17, who has Juvenile Batten Disease, recently benefited from advice from the Financial Wellbeing and Energy Advice (FWEA) service, which has helped save families over £2m over the past two years. “When you have a child with complex needs who relies on a lot of electrical equipment such as a feeding pump and an electric bed and an overhead hoist, costs add up,” says Valerie, from Edinburgh . Valerie Trayner with Kayden who has Juvenile Batten Disease (Image: CHAS) “The FWEA team have helped me in many ways – by going through our family finances, suggesting ways in which savings could be made and informing us about funding and benefits we could apply – many of which we did not even realise we were entitled to. “Thanks to the support we are now in a much more comfortable position financially which has relieved a lot of stress and means we can look forward to Christmas this year.” CHAS CEO Rami Okasha says: “There are thousands of families across Scotland having to deal with the unthinkable reality that their child may die young. “CHAS provides expert medical, nursing, and social work care for families facing the most difficult times of their lives. Valerie Trayner says she has received advice from CHAS to help with costs involved in Kayden's care (Image: CHAS) “We remain utterly focused on being there for families at every stage of their palliative care journeys, from the moment a parent learns their child is seriously ill and may die young, helping them live well, and providing dignified end-of-life care. “CHAS provides expert medical, nursing, and social work care for families facing the most difficult times of their lives. “We’re seeing more people needing urgent support and, without immediate action, we simply won’t be able to meet this growing demand. “We know we can’t reach everyone who needs us without the kindness and generosity of our supporters, so we are asking the Scottish public for their help by donating to our Christmas appeal.” To donate to CHAS’s The Christmas That Couldn’t Wait Appeal visit: www.chas.org.uk/appeal CHAS Charity Children's Hospices Around Scotland Children's Health Christmas Charity Health People Dumbarton Dumfries Edinburgh Glenrothes Perth Scotland Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... Thursday 30 October 2025 20:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 3:46 \'They have scandal after scandal\' Why you can trust Sky News Kemi Badenoch has said hacking into Harriet Harman\'s website when she was younger is "not the same" as Rachel Reeves failing to get a £900 rental licence for her home. The Tory leader, who has called for the chancellor to go for breaking the law, told Sky News\' deputy political editor Sam Coates she was not an MP in 2008 when she got into Labour peer Baroness Harman\'s website and changed it so it was pro-Conservative. Politics latest: Reeves told she has to go after breaking law Hacking into websites is a criminal offence and can be punishable with a fine or up to a two-year prison sentence for minor offences, or life imprisonment for the most serious. Asked if she had ever broken the law, Ms Badenoch said: "I don\'t believe that I have, but if I had done so, if I had done so when I was in government, then I would have been sacked or I would have been forced to resign." But reminded of her hacking episode, she said: "This was something I did in my 20s. "We\'re not talking about something that Rachel Reeves did in her 20s, we\'re talking about something she\'s doing as chancellor, after she became chancellor. "It is not the same thing at all." She said people should not "try and draw a false equivalence" and said she guessed Baroness Harman\'s password to enter the website, adding it was "a summary offence, like speeding". "This is whataboutery, we have a government of people who are repeatedly breaking the law," she added. Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 2:20 Harman recalls Badenoch hacking her website Ms Reeves has said she was not aware she needed a rental licence , required in some areas, to let out her family home in Dulwich, southeast London, after she moved to Downing Street when she was made chancellor. The estate agents she used, Harvey & Wheeler, have since apologised and confirmed they said they would organise the licence and then failed to do so, after a member of staff left. Emails released by Downing Street show Ms Reeves\' husband agreeing to this with the company. The chancellor maintained her apology to the prime minister, saying she should have been aware of the details of the situation. Prior to the full details coming to light, Ms Badenoch said Ms Reeves\'s position is untenable, given the PM has said "lawbreakers shouldn\'t be lawmakers". Read more: What law has Rachel Reeves broken? What are rental licensing laws? Under the Housing Act 2004, introduced by Labour, councils can decide to introduce selective licensing, where residential landlords in specified areas must have a licence. Landlords must adhere to certain requirements to obtain a licence, including gas certificates, working carbon monoxide alarms and fire safety regulations for furnishings. They must secure a licence within 28 days of renting out a home. Southwark Council, where Rachel Reeves\' house is, charges £900 for a licence, which lasts five years. Failure to secure a selective licence can result in a penalty of up to £30,000 or an unlimited fine from a court upon conviction.
